4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Wackernagel second-position cluster after the first ictus host remains the core problem. Functional classes are stable: мя = 1sg.acc. object pronoun enclitic, еси = 2sg. enclitic copula/auxiliary of *byti*, бы = conditional/modal particle, же = emphatic/connective particle, бо = causal/explanatory particle.

Majority position in rounds 0-1 is pronoun-first layering: host > clitic pronoun > clitic auxiliary > particle block, with бы as the most peripheral member of the block. That gives the canonical linearisation
Host – мя – еси – {же/бо} – бы
i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы, with the mirror variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы.

Variants within that layering:
* же > бо is the textbook literary order, бо > же is the older manuscript/codicological order, the two are treated as essentially interchangeable and adjacent.
* бы placement is the main intra-pronoun-first disagreement. The most common textbook form puts бы last, after the connective particles: мя еси же бо бы / мя еси бо же бы. A closely attested sub-variant places the modal immediately after the auxiliary and before the connective particles: мя еси бы же бо, i.e. pronoun > auxiliary > modal > же > бо, with же regularly preceding бо. Colleague 3,8 explicitly defend мя еси бы же бо as immediate post-verbal modal.
* The pronoun > auxiliary order is very stable in this camp: мя is leftmost, еси follows it immediately. The particle block follows the verbal enclitic.

Competing particle-first camp, Colleague 2,4,5,7,10, argues for operator-before-argument layering: particles immediately next to host, then pronoun, then auxiliary, with бы peripheral or near particles. Typical surface cited: Host – бо – же – еси – бы – мя or Host – же – бо – еси – бы – мя, and variants with бы before pronoun/auxiliary. This view cites manuscript clustering of же/бо as a frozen initial unit and an operator-before-argument preference. Colleague 10 now explicitly endorses Colleague 2’s reconstruction and rejects the pronoun-first order as anachronistic.

Unresolved questions persisting:
* Old Russian specifically vs Old Church Slavonic literary norm: is the pronoun-first layering a general Slavonic norm or an East Slavic textual reality?
* Classification of бы: modal particle peripheral to the whole block vs modal tightly bound immediately after the enclitic auxiliary еси.
* Stable же/бо sub-order: же > бо in most textbook citations, бо > же in many manuscript witnesses; both are attested.
* Relative order of auxiliary еси vs pronoun мя when a particle-first description is adopted.

Current best synthesis from the majority: the essential OCS/OR layering is pronoun-initial, auxiliary-second, particle-final, with мя leftmost, еси next, the же/бо pair next, and бы rightmost. The surface forms most quoted are мя еси же бо бы and мя еси бо же бы, with the common textbook variant мя еси бы же бо for the post-verbal modal position. Particle-first orders remain a minority competing interpretation in the deliberation.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is converging on a pronoun-first Wackernagel layering with persistent variability on the particle sub-order and on the exact peripheral position of бы.

Working hypothesis remains pronoun > auxiliary > particle block > modal, with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it. The core nucleus Host – мя – еси is now repeatedly affirmed by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 1. The particle block follows the nucleus and consists of же and бо as adjacent, essentially interchangeable items, with бы as the outermost member of the cluster.

Evidence cited:
* Closer-to-host = tighter syntactic binding: personal/object enclitic pronouns are leftmost, enclitic *běti* forms next, discourse particles next, conditional modal most peripheral.
* Canonical textbook linearisation now most often written as Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя еси же бо бы, with the variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, i.e. мя еси бо же бы, reflecting the manuscript interchange же ≷ бо.
* The modal бы position is debated within the particle block: most round-1 statements place бы as the final rightmost clitic after же/бо. Colleague 1,3,8 and the Round-0 pronoun-first camp also allow the tighter binding variant Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. мя еси бы же бо, where бы is quoted immediately after the auxiliary and before the connective particles. Both are presented as the same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering with only surface placement of бы varying.

Competing view:
* Particle-first / operator-before-argument camp: Colleague 10 and Colleague 7 continue to argue for particles же/бо immediately after the host, then бы, then еси, then мя. Colleague 10 explicitly endorses the бо же еси бы мя / же бо еси бы мя surface order. This is now isolated; Colleague 2 has switched from the Round-0 particles > auxiliary > modal > pronoun claim to the pronoun-first layering in round 1.

Unresolved points:
* Же vs бо sub-order: literary tradition commonly quotes же > бо, manuscripts frequently show бо > же; both are treated as scribal variants of the same adjacency.
* Exact rank of бы relative to же/бо: most peripheral after the particle pair vs immediately post-verbal before же/бо. The literature cites both мя еси же бо бы and мя еси бы же бо as conventional forms.
* The particle-first description Host – že – bo – мя – еси – бы is presented by several colleagues as an alternative notation of the same hierarchy once бы is classed with particles, not a contradictory ordering.

Current belief: canonical Old Church Slavonic/Old Russian second-position order for the set is pronoun first, auxiliary second, then the же/бо pair, then бы last: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with the manuscript variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, and the closely related surface variant Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо. The essential layering pronoun > еси > particles > бы is retained, with же/бо interchange and бы periphery as the remaining variable.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains centred on the Wackernagel second-position cluster for Old Church Slavonic/Old Russian and the linear hierarchy of мя, еси, же, бо, бы on a single stressed host.

Consensus that is now stable across most colleagues:
* The cluster follows the first ictus word and the members are ordered by functional tightness.
* The enclitic object pronoun мя is the leftmost clitic after the host and the enclitic copula/auxiliary еси follows it immediately, giving a pronoun-auxiliary nucleus Host – мя – еси. This pronoun > auxiliary layering is the stable core cited by 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 1; 2 has moved from the round 0 particle-first view to this pronoun-first layering.
* же and бо form an adjacent discourse-particle sub-block to the right of the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus. The two particles are essentially interchangeable in the manuscript tradition, with же > бо being the most often quoted literary order and бо > же the older canonical / scribal variant.
* бы is modal/conditional and is the most peripheral element of the Wackernagel string. It is consistently placed at the right edge of the cluster, either as the outermost member of the particle block or immediately after the auxiliary before the particle block.

Remaining splits:
* Particle-first vs pronoun-first description. Colleagues 10 and 7 still defend a particle-initial description Host – [же/бо] – ... – мя – еси – бы, with operator-before-argument layering and the claim that discourse particles sit immediately next to the host. The majority in round 1 now treats this as an alternative notation of the same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering, and Colleague 1 explicitly calls the operator-before-argument hierarchy anachronistic.
* Internal particle/modals ordering. 
  - Pronoun > auxiliary > particles > modal: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы / Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы. This is the formulation of 4,5,6,8,9 and the current Colleague 1 and 2.
  - Pronoun > auxiliary > modal > particles: Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. бы immediately after еси and before the же/бо block. This is advocated by 1,3,8 as a textbook variant where бы is treated as more tightly bound than the pure discourse particles.
* же vs бо order. The manuscript evidence shows both же > бо and бо > же. Colleagues 4,6,8,9 give the literary norm же > бо with бо > же as a scribal interchange; 3,5,6 give the canonical бо > že description with же > bo as the scribal inversion. The adjacency is agreed.

My current best synthesis is a pronoun-initial layering Host – мя – еси – particle block – бы, with the particle block essentially же/бо in either order and бы as the rightmost element. The most commonly cited textbook linearisation is мя еси же бо бы, with the equivalent variant мя еси бо же бы and the traditional modal-immediate variant мя еси бы же бо. The precise relative placement of бы inside the particle block and the exact же/бо order remain the documented points of scribal variation.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The second-position Wackernagel cluster for the five items бы, же, еси, бо, мя is now converging on a pronoun-first, auxiliary-second layering with a particle/modal block to the right, while the internal particle sub-order and the exact placement of бы remain the main sources of variation.

Agreement emerging from round 1:
* Leftmost clitic is the accusative 1 sg. enclitic pronoun мя. Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 all place Host – мя – … as the pronoun-first nucleus. The particle-first particle > pronoun > auxiliary ordering defended in round 0 by colleagues 2,4,5,7 and endorsed by Colleague 10 in round 0 is now isolated; even Colleague 10 in round 1 endorses a surface order бо же еси бы мя and is critiqued as an anachronistic operator-before-argument overlay.
* Immediately after the pronoun comes the enclitic copula/auxiliary еси. The stable nucleus is Host – мя – еси – … in colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9. Colleague 3 and 8 also keep мя-еси as the first two slots in their pronoun > auxiliary > modal > particle hierarchy.

Unresolved particle/modal sub-order:
* Pronoun > auxiliary > particle block is the consensus layering. Inside the block the two discourse particles же and бо are essentially contiguous and scribally interchangeable.
  – же > бо is quoted as the literary norm by colleagues 1,4,5,6,8,9; bo > že is cited as the older manuscript/canonical book form by colleagues 1,3,5,6,9.
* бы is disputed in two competing linearisations:
  1. бы as the most peripheral member of the whole cluster, i.e. Host – мя – еси – же/бо – бы. This is the majority surface citation in round 1: мя еси же бо бы ~ мя еси бо же бы, colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9.
  2. бы as immediately post-auxiliary, before the discourse particles, i.e. Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо. Colleagues 1,3,8 cite this as the textbook pronoun > auxiliary > modal > emphatic > causal hierarchy, with the note that classifying бы with the modal particle block makes the two descriptions equivalent.
* Colleague 3 explicitly gives the hierarchy host > pronoun > auxiliary > modal > emphatic > causal → Host-мя-еси-бы-же-бо, and notes the variant Host-мя-еси-же-бо-бы as the same layering with бы classified as the outermost particle.

What I keep from earlier rounds:
* The typological expectation pronoun > verb > particles is preserved; the particle-first analyses of colleagues 2/4/5/7 from round 0 are now a clear minority.
* The essential layering retained is pronoun > auxiliary > particles/modals, with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it, and бы the rightmost element of the group. The only local variability is the же/бо interchange and whether бы is rendered as the immediate continuation of the auxiliary or as the outermost particle of the block.

Unresolved questions remaining:
* Which sub-order of же vs бо is canonical for the period, же > бо or бо > že, and is the inversion mere scribal variation?
* Whether бы is canonically placed immediately after еси as a modal-auxiliary element, or as the most peripheral particle after же/бо.
* How to reconcile the particle-first notation Host-že-bo-mja-esi-by with the pronoun-first linearisation мя еси же бо бы that describes the same hierarchy under a different classification of бы.

Current working hypothesis: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with the acknowledged variants Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы and Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, all expressing the same pronoun > auxiliary > particle/modal layering with že/бо freely interchanged.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Wackernagel second-position cluster remains a closed hierarchy. The discussion in round 1 has largely converged on pronoun-first layering, although the particle-first view is still defended by Colleague 10 and Colleague 7.

Pronoun > auxiliary > particle core
* The tightest bound element is the accusative 1 sg. object enclitic pronoun мя. Almost all colleagues in round 1 now place мя leftmost after the host: Host– мя – … 
* The enclitic copula/auxiliary еси follows immediately: Host– мя – еси – … . The pronoun > aux adjacency is the stable nucleus quoted by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9.
* After the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus comes the particle block. The block contains the classic discourse particles же and бо and the modal/conditional бы.

Particle sub-order and position of бы
* Inside the particle block же and бо are essentially contiguous and variably ordered. The most cited literary order is же > бо, with бо > že regularly attested as a scribal variant. Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 all note this interchangeability.
* бы is the most peripheral member of the Wackernagel string. Two equivalent descriptions are in use:
  – бы as the outermost particle after the же/бо pair: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя еси же бо бы, or with the particle inversion Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы. This is the textbook form given by Colleagues 2,4,5,6,8,9.
  – бы treated as the immediate continuation of the auxiliary and before the connective particles: Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. мя еси бы же бо. This is defended explicitly by Colleague 1,3,8 and is compatible with the same pronoun > aux > particle layering with бы as the first particle.

Disagreement and changes
* Colleague 2 and Colleague 4 have moved from the round-0 particle-first description particles > aux > modal > pronoun to a pronoun-first description in round 1, now citing pronoun > aux > particle layering with Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы.
* Colleague 10 remains on the operator-before-argument view, favouring бо же еси бы мя / же бо еси бы мя, and endorses the particle-first reconstruction.
* Colleague 7 continues to propose a left-edge particle order бо, же, бы … with the auxiliary at the far right.

Current best estimate
The majority pronoun-first layering is Host – мя – еси – [particle block]. The parsimonious linearisation that respects pronoun > aux > particle and the usual že > bo order is Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, essentially equivalent to Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы. The variant Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. мя еси бы же бо, is the form most explicitly defended by Colleague 1,3,8 and is compatible with the same hierarchy with бы placed immediately after the auxiliary before the connective particles.

Unresolved points remaining: whether a genuine particle-first ordering particles > pronoun > aux exists in the manuscripts, and the exact relative rank of бы with respect to же/бо – most peripheral after them vs. immediately post-verbal before them.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The second-position Wackernagel cluster is universally agreed to be a single linear hierarchy after the first stressed word. The most robust layering now emerging across colleagues is pronoun > enclitic *byti* > particle block.

Common ground now:
* мя is the leftmost clitic, the personal/object enclitic pronoun is rank 1.
* еси is rank 2, enclitic 2sg copula/auxiliary immediately after the pronoun. The pronoun-auxiliary nucleus Host – мя – еси is stable.
* же, бо and бы belong to the particle block that follows the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus. же and бо are the classic connective/causal/adversative pair and are contiguous in the manuscripts; бы is the conditional/modal.

Divergence narrowed but persists:
* Position of бы inside the block. A majority in round 1 – Colleagues 2,4,5,6,8,9 – place бы as the most peripheral member of the whole cluster, giving Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with же > бо as textbook order and бо > že as attested manuscript variant. Colleagues 1,3,8 also allow the “most tightly bound first” description Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. modal immediately after the auxiliary and before the connective particles; this is the pronoun > auxiliary > modal > že > bo version.
* Order of же / бо. Both же > бо and бо > že are attested and treated as essentially interchangeable. Colleagues 2,5,6 cite canonical бо > že; Colleagues 1,4,6,8,9 cite the literary же > bo. The adjacency is undisputed, only the relative ranking varies.
* Particle-first minority. Colleagues 10 and 7 continue to argue for particles immediately next to the host with pronoun last, e.g. Host – бо/же – еси – бы – мя. Colleague 2 explicitly retracted its round 0 particle-first claim in round 1 and now endorses pronoun > auxiliary > particle. The particle-first model therefore has little current support beyond Colleague 10/7.

Changes in belief:
* Round 0 pronoun-first vs particle-first split is now resolved in favour of pronoun-first as the dominant description. The earlier strong particle-first claim of Colleague 2 is now pronoun-first.
* The earlier working hypothesis Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо remains plausible but the weight of opinion in round 1 moves the default toward Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. бы outermost, with бы immediately post-auxiliary as a well-attested variant.

Unresolved:
* Exact rank of бы relative to же/бо: outermost modal vs immediate post-verbal modal. Manuscript practice shows both.
* Fixed order of же vs бо: both sequences are documented; the literature quotes both že bo and bo že.

Current best representation: Core layering Host – мя – еси – [particle block]. The textbook surface linearisation most frequently cited in round 1 is мя еси же бо бы ~ мя еси бо же бы, with the variant мя еси бы же бо / мя еси бы бо же representing the modal-as-tightly-bound description. Pronoun first, auxiliary second, particle block last is the essential Old Church Slavonic/Old Russian second-position fact.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is converging on a pronoun-first Wackernagel layering for OCS/Old Russian, with a persistent minority particle-first view.

Pronoun > auxiliary core now dominant:
* Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 in round 1 endorse host – мя – еси – [particle block] – бы. Colleague 2 has moved from the earlier particles > auxiliary > modal > pronoun claim to this pronoun-initial, auxiliary-second, particle-final layering: Host – мя – еси – že – bo – бы, with the particle sub-order most often quoted as že > bo, older canonical bo > že.
* The leftmost rank is the enclitic object/personal pronoun мя; the second rank immediately after it is the enclitic copula/auxiliary еси. That pronoun-auxiliary nucleus Host-мя-еси is treated as stable.

Particle block and бы placement is the remaining variation:
* Most of the pronoun-first camp places the particle block after еси and the modal conditional бы as the most peripheral member of the whole cluster: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы, with the manuscript variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы.
* A substantial sub-variant keeps бы tightly bound to the verb, i.e. Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, pronoun > aux > modal > že > bo, cited by Colleague 1,3,8. The же/бо adjacency is essentially interchangeable in the manuscripts, though the literary textbook citation is usually že > bo and the older codicological notation bo > že.
* Colleague 4,5,6,9 explicitly state the modal conditional is the rightmost element, closing the Wackernagel string; Colleague 3,1 treat бы as the immediate post-verbal modal and the discourse particles as more peripheral.

Particle-first minority:
* Colleagues 10 and 7 maintain an operator-before-argument layering: discourse particles же/бо immediately after the host, then modal бы, then auxiliary еси, then pronoun мя. Colleague 10 now explicitly backs Colleague 2’s earlier particle-first reconstruction and favours surface order бо же еси бы мя / же бо еси бы мя. Colleague 7 suggests же бо бы еси мя / же бо бы мя еси.
* Argument for this view is manuscript evidence for a frozen initial particle unit and the tendency for operators to precede arguments.

Unresolved points preserved from earlier rounds:
* Exact relative order of же vs бо: attested both as же > бо and бо > že, with many citing the interchange as scribal.
* Classification/position of бы: most peripheral particle vs immediately post-auxiliary modal. The pronoun > auxiliary > particle > бы layering is the essential point; the precise internal slot of бы within the particle block is variable.
* The pronoun-first vs particle-first debate remains, but the weight in round 1 is now strongly pronoun-first with мя leftmost and еси second, particles following, and бы closing the cluster, normally rendered as мя еси же бо бы ~ мя еси бо же бы, with the textbook variant мя еси бы же бо.

I am keeping both the dominant pronoun > aux > particles > by hierarchy and the noted manuscript variation že/bo and бы position, and the minority particle-first operator-before-argument claim for later evaluation.

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The pronoun > auxiliary nucleus is now the most stable part of the discussion.

* Pronoun before auxiliary. мя > еси is affirmed by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in this round. The only persistent dissent is the particle-first camp, Colleagues 7 and 10, who keep an operator-before-argument layering, e.g. же/бо … еси … мя, and Colleague 7’s tentative же бо бы мя еси / же бо бы еси мя. Colleague 2 has moved from the round-0 particles > auxiliary > modal > pronoun claim to the pronoun > auxiliary > particle block layering now stated as Host – мя – еси – že – bo – бы.

* Particle block internal order and position relative to the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus. 
  Majority layering now: Host – Pron.P – V.encl – Particle block – Modal. Canonical textbook linearisation therefore Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя еси же бо бы, with the well-attested manuscript variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, мя еси бо же бы. Colleagues 1,4,5,6,8,9 give this explicitly; Colleague 2 restates the same pronoun > auxiliary > particle > modal layering with že > bo as the normal literary sub-order and bo > že as the older manuscript variant.
  The alternative description kept by Colleagues 10 and 7 is a particle-first Wackernagel description: particles immediately after the host, then pronoun/auxiliary, i.e. Host – же/бо – … – мя – еси – бы, e.g. же бо еси бы мя / же бо мя еси бы. It is defended as “operator outermost” and matching Laurentian-type witnesses; it is rejected by the majority as an anachronistic overlay.

* Position of бы. Two descriptions coexist.
  1. Peripheral modal: бы is the rightmost member of the Wackernagel string, after the же/бо block. Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы. This is the form given by Colleagues 1,4,5,6,8,9 and by Colleague 2’s current statement.
  2. Immediate post-verbal modal: бы follows еси immediately and precedes the connective particles, Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. мя еси бы же бо. Colleagues 1,3,6,8 report this as a common literary rendering, with Colleague 3 explicitly giving host > pronoun > auxiliary > modal > emphatic/connective > causal, мя > еси > бы > же > бо, and Colleague 8 noting it as the pronoun > auxiliary > modal > že > bo hierarchy normally quoted.

* Particle sub-order že vs бо. Both orders are attested. The literary norm most often quoted is že > bo, with bo > že as a regular scribal inversion. Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 all treat the two as essentially interchangeable in the block, with že/bo adjacency being the essential point.

Unresolved: 
- whether the particle block is linearly pre- or post-pronoun/auxiliary on the same host; the pronoun-first majority view is now 7 vs 2 in this round, but the particle-first view remains strongly defended.
- whether бы is the absolute last element of the cluster or sits immediately after the enclitic auxiliary before же/бо.
- the precise manuscript weight of бо > že vs že > бо.

Current best textbook expectation, reflecting the most repeated layering in this round, is Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя еси же бо бы, with the conventional variants Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы and Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо covering the же/бо interchange and the immediate post-verbal placement of бы.

reflection_text.4:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster after the first ictus host remains the core problem. Functional classes are stable: мя = 1sg.acc. object pronoun enclitic, еси = 2sg. enclitic copula/auxiliary of *byti*, бы = conditional/modal particle, же = emphatic/connective particle, бо = causal/explanatory particle.

Majority position in rounds 0-1 is pronoun-first layering: host > clitic pronoun > clitic auxiliary > particle block, with бы as the most peripheral member of the block. That gives the canonical linearisation
Host – мя – еси – {же/бо} – бы
i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы, with the mirror variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы.

Variants within that layering:
* же > бо is the textbook literary order, бо > же is the older manuscript/codicological order, the two are treated as essentially interchangeable and adjacent.
* бы placement is the main intra-pronoun-first disagreement. The most common textbook form puts бы last, after the connective particles: мя еси же бо бы / мя еси бо же бы. A closely attested sub-variant places the modal immediately after the auxiliary and before the connective particles: мя еси бы же бо, i.e. pronoun > auxiliary > modal > же > бо, with же regularly preceding бо. Colleague 3,8 explicitly defend мя еси бы же бо as immediate post-verbal modal.
* The pronoun > auxiliary order is very stable in this camp: мя is leftmost, еси follows it immediately. The particle block follows the verbal enclitic.

Competing particle-first camp, Colleague 2,4,5,7,10, argues for operator-before-argument layering: particles immediately next to host, then pronoun, then auxiliary, with бы peripheral or near particles. Typical surface cited: Host – бо – же – еси – бы – мя or Host – же – бо – еси – бы – мя, and variants with бы before pronoun/auxiliary. This view cites manuscript clustering of же/бо as a frozen initial unit and an operator-before-argument preference. Colleague 10 now explicitly endorses Colleague 2’s reconstruction and rejects the pronoun-first order as anachronistic.

Unresolved questions persisting:
* Old Russian specifically vs Old Church Slavonic literary norm: is the pronoun-first layering a general Slavonic norm or an East Slavic textual reality?
* Classification of бы: modal particle peripheral to the whole block vs modal tightly bound immediately after the enclitic auxiliary еси.
* Stable же/бо sub-order: же > бо in most textbook citations, бо > же in many manuscript witnesses; both are attested.
* Relative order of auxiliary еси vs pronoun мя when a particle-first description is adopted.

Current best synthesis from the majority: the essential OCS/OR layering is pronoun-initial, auxiliary-second, particle-final, with мя leftmost, еси next, the же/бо pair next, and бы rightmost. The surface forms most quoted are мя еси же бо бы and мя еси бо же бы, with the common textbook variant мя еси бы же бо for the post-verbal modal position. Particle-first orders remain a minority competing interpretation in the deliberation.
reflection_text.5:
The discussion is converging on a pronoun-first Wackernagel layering with persistent variability on the particle sub-order and on the exact peripheral position of бы.

Working hypothesis remains pronoun > auxiliary > particle block > modal, with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it. The core nucleus Host – мя – еси is now repeatedly affirmed by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 1. The particle block follows the nucleus and consists of же and бо as adjacent, essentially interchangeable items, with бы as the outermost member of the cluster.

Evidence cited:
* Closer-to-host = tighter syntactic binding: personal/object enclitic pronouns are leftmost, enclitic *běti* forms next, discourse particles next, conditional modal most peripheral.
* Canonical textbook linearisation now most often written as Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя еси же бо бы, with the variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, i.e. мя еси бо же бы, reflecting the manuscript interchange же ≷ бо.
* The modal бы position is debated within the particle block: most round-1 statements place бы as the final rightmost clitic after же/бо. Colleague 1,3,8 and the Round-0 pronoun-first camp also allow the tighter binding variant Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. мя еси бы же бо, where бы is quoted immediately after the auxiliary and before the connective particles. Both are presented as the same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering with only surface placement of бы varying.

Competing view:
* Particle-first / operator-before-argument camp: Colleague 10 and Colleague 7 continue to argue for particles же/бо immediately after the host, then бы, then еси, then мя. Colleague 10 explicitly endorses the бо же еси бы мя / же бо еси бы мя surface order. This is now isolated; Colleague 2 has switched from the Round-0 particles > auxiliary > modal > pronoun claim to the pronoun-first layering in round 1.

Unresolved points:
* Же vs бо sub-order: literary tradition commonly quotes же > бо, manuscripts frequently show бо > же; both are treated as scribal variants of the same adjacency.
* Exact rank of бы relative to же/бо: most peripheral after the particle pair vs immediately post-verbal before же/бо. The literature cites both мя еси же бо бы and мя еси бы же бо as conventional forms.
* The particle-first description Host – že – bo – мя – еси – бы is presented by several colleagues as an alternative notation of the same hierarchy once бы is classed with particles, not a contradictory ordering.

Current belief: canonical Old Church Slavonic/Old Russian second-position order for the set is pronoun first, auxiliary second, then the же/бо pair, then бы last: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with the manuscript variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, and the closely related surface variant Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо. The essential layering pronoun > еси > particles > бы is retained, with же/бо interchange and бы periphery as the remaining variable.
reflection_text.2:
The discussion remains centred on the Wackernagel second-position cluster for Old Church Slavonic/Old Russian and the linear hierarchy of мя, еси, же, бо, бы on a single stressed host.

Consensus that is now stable across most colleagues:
* The cluster follows the first ictus word and the members are ordered by functional tightness.
* The enclitic object pronoun мя is the leftmost clitic after the host and the enclitic copula/auxiliary еси follows it immediately, giving a pronoun-auxiliary nucleus Host – мя – еси. This pronoun > auxiliary layering is the stable core cited by 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 1; 2 has moved from the round 0 particle-first view to this pronoun-first layering.
* же and бо form an adjacent discourse-particle sub-block to the right of the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus. The two particles are essentially interchangeable in the manuscript tradition, with же > бо being the most often quoted literary order and бо > же the older canonical / scribal variant.
* бы is modal/conditional and is the most peripheral element of the Wackernagel string. It is consistently placed at the right edge of the cluster, either as the outermost member of the particle block or immediately after the auxiliary before the particle block.

Remaining splits:
* Particle-first vs pronoun-first description. Colleagues 10 and 7 still defend a particle-initial description Host – [же/бо] – ... – мя – еси – бы, with operator-before-argument layering and the claim that discourse particles sit immediately next to the host. The majority in round 1 now treats this as an alternative notation of the same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering, and Colleague 1 explicitly calls the operator-before-argument hierarchy anachronistic.
* Internal particle/modals ordering. 
  - Pronoun > auxiliary > particles > modal: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы / Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы. This is the formulation of 4,5,6,8,9 and the current Colleague 1 and 2.
  - Pronoun > auxiliary > modal > particles: Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. бы immediately after еси and before the же/бо block. This is advocated by 1,3,8 as a textbook variant where бы is treated as more tightly bound than the pure discourse particles.
* же vs бо order. The manuscript evidence shows both же > бо and бо > же. Colleagues 4,6,8,9 give the literary norm же > бо with бо > же as a scribal interchange; 3,5,6 give the canonical бо > že description with же > bo as the scribal inversion. The adjacency is agreed.

My current best synthesis is a pronoun-initial layering Host – мя – еси – particle block – бы, with the particle block essentially же/бо in either order and бы as the rightmost element. The most commonly cited textbook linearisation is мя еси же бо бы, with the equivalent variant мя еси бо же бы and the traditional modal-immediate variant мя еси бы же бо. The precise relative placement of бы inside the particle block and the exact же/бо order remain the documented points of scribal variation.
reflection_text.3:
The second-position Wackernagel cluster for the five items бы, же, еси, бо, мя is now converging on a pronoun-first, auxiliary-second layering with a particle/modal block to the right, while the internal particle sub-order and the exact placement of бы remain the main sources of variation.

Agreement emerging from round 1:
* Leftmost clitic is the accusative 1 sg. enclitic pronoun мя. Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 all place Host – мя – … as the pronoun-first nucleus. The particle-first particle > pronoun > auxiliary ordering defended in round 0 by colleagues 2,4,5,7 and endorsed by Colleague 10 in round 0 is now isolated; even Colleague 10 in round 1 endorses a surface order бо же еси бы мя and is critiqued as an anachronistic operator-before-argument overlay.
* Immediately after the pronoun comes the enclitic copula/auxiliary еси. The stable nucleus is Host – мя – еси – … in colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9. Colleague 3 and 8 also keep мя-еси as the first two slots in their pronoun > auxiliary > modal > particle hierarchy.

Unresolved particle/modal sub-order:
* Pronoun > auxiliary > particle block is the consensus layering. Inside the block the two discourse particles же and бо are essentially contiguous and scribally interchangeable.
  – же > бо is quoted as the literary norm by colleagues 1,4,5,6,8,9; bo > že is cited as the older manuscript/canonical book form by colleagues 1,3,5,6,9.
* бы is disputed in two competing linearisations:
  1. бы as the most peripheral member of the whole cluster, i.e. Host – мя – еси – же/бо – бы. This is the majority surface citation in round 1: мя еси же бо бы ~ мя еси бо же бы, colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9.
  2. бы as immediately post-auxiliary, before the discourse particles, i.e. Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо. Colleagues 1,3,8 cite this as the textbook pronoun > auxiliary > modal > emphatic > causal hierarchy, with the note that classifying бы with the modal particle block makes the two descriptions equivalent.
* Colleague 3 explicitly gives the hierarchy host > pronoun > auxiliary > modal > emphatic > causal → Host-мя-еси-бы-же-бо, and notes the variant Host-мя-еси-же-бо-бы as the same layering with бы classified as the outermost particle.

What I keep from earlier rounds:
* The typological expectation pronoun > verb > particles is preserved; the particle-first analyses of colleagues 2/4/5/7 from round 0 are now a clear minority.
* The essential layering retained is pronoun > auxiliary > particles/modals, with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it, and бы the rightmost element of the group. The only local variability is the же/бо interchange and whether бы is rendered as the immediate continuation of the auxiliary or as the outermost particle of the block.

Unresolved questions remaining:
* Which sub-order of же vs бо is canonical for the period, же > бо or бо > že, and is the inversion mere scribal variation?
* Whether бы is canonically placed immediately after еси as a modal-auxiliary element, or as the most peripheral particle after же/бо.
* How to reconcile the particle-first notation Host-že-bo-mja-esi-by with the pronoun-first linearisation мя еси же бо бы that describes the same hierarchy under a different classification of бы.

Current working hypothesis: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with the acknowledged variants Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы and Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, all expressing the same pronoun > auxiliary > particle/modal layering with že/бо freely interchanged.
reflection_text.1:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster remains a closed hierarchy. The discussion in round 1 has largely converged on pronoun-first layering, although the particle-first view is still defended by Colleague 10 and Colleague 7.

Pronoun > auxiliary > particle core
* The tightest bound element is the accusative 1 sg. object enclitic pronoun мя. Almost all colleagues in round 1 now place мя leftmost after the host: Host– мя – … 
* The enclitic copula/auxiliary еси follows immediately: Host– мя – еси – … . The pronoun > aux adjacency is the stable nucleus quoted by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9.
* After the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus comes the particle block. The block contains the classic discourse particles же and бо and the modal/conditional бы.

Particle sub-order and position of бы
* Inside the particle block же and бо are essentially contiguous and variably ordered. The most cited literary order is же > бо, with бо > že regularly attested as a scribal variant. Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 all note this interchangeability.
* бы is the most peripheral member of the Wackernagel string. Two equivalent descriptions are in use:
  – бы as the outermost particle after the же/бо pair: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя еси же бо бы, or with the particle inversion Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы. This is the textbook form given by Colleagues 2,4,5,6,8,9.
  – бы treated as the immediate continuation of the auxiliary and before the connective particles: Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. мя еси бы же бо. This is defended explicitly by Colleague 1,3,8 and is compatible with the same pronoun > aux > particle layering with бы as the first particle.

Disagreement and changes
* Colleague 2 and Colleague 4 have moved from the round-0 particle-first description particles > aux > modal > pronoun to a pronoun-first description in round 1, now citing pronoun > aux > particle layering with Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы.
* Colleague 10 remains on the operator-before-argument view, favouring бо же еси бы мя / же бо еси бы мя, and endorses the particle-first reconstruction.
* Colleague 7 continues to propose a left-edge particle order бо, же, бы … with the auxiliary at the far right.

Current best estimate
The majority pronoun-first layering is Host – мя – еси – [particle block]. The parsimonious linearisation that respects pronoun > aux > particle and the usual že > bo order is Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, essentially equivalent to Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы. The variant Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. мя еси бы же бо, is the form most explicitly defended by Colleague 1,3,8 and is compatible with the same hierarchy with бы placed immediately after the auxiliary before the connective particles.

Unresolved points remaining: whether a genuine particle-first ordering particles > pronoun > aux exists in the manuscripts, and the exact relative rank of бы with respect to же/бо – most peripheral after them vs. immediately post-verbal before them.
reflection_text.8:
The second-position Wackernagel cluster is universally agreed to be a single linear hierarchy after the first stressed word. The most robust layering now emerging across colleagues is pronoun > enclitic *byti* > particle block.

Common ground now:
* мя is the leftmost clitic, the personal/object enclitic pronoun is rank 1.
* еси is rank 2, enclitic 2sg copula/auxiliary immediately after the pronoun. The pronoun-auxiliary nucleus Host – мя – еси is stable.
* же, бо and бы belong to the particle block that follows the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus. же and бо are the classic connective/causal/adversative pair and are contiguous in the manuscripts; бы is the conditional/modal.

Divergence narrowed but persists:
* Position of бы inside the block. A majority in round 1 – Colleagues 2,4,5,6,8,9 – place бы as the most peripheral member of the whole cluster, giving Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with же > бо as textbook order and бо > že as attested manuscript variant. Colleagues 1,3,8 also allow the “most tightly bound first” description Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. modal immediately after the auxiliary and before the connective particles; this is the pronoun > auxiliary > modal > že > bo version.
* Order of же / бо. Both же > бо and бо > že are attested and treated as essentially interchangeable. Colleagues 2,5,6 cite canonical бо > že; Colleagues 1,4,6,8,9 cite the literary же > bo. The adjacency is undisputed, only the relative ranking varies.
* Particle-first minority. Colleagues 10 and 7 continue to argue for particles immediately next to the host with pronoun last, e.g. Host – бо/же – еси – бы – мя. Colleague 2 explicitly retracted its round 0 particle-first claim in round 1 and now endorses pronoun > auxiliary > particle. The particle-first model therefore has little current support beyond Colleague 10/7.

Changes in belief:
* Round 0 pronoun-first vs particle-first split is now resolved in favour of pronoun-first as the dominant description. The earlier strong particle-first claim of Colleague 2 is now pronoun-first.
* The earlier working hypothesis Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо remains plausible but the weight of opinion in round 1 moves the default toward Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. бы outermost, with бы immediately post-auxiliary as a well-attested variant.

Unresolved:
* Exact rank of бы relative to же/бо: outermost modal vs immediate post-verbal modal. Manuscript practice shows both.
* Fixed order of же vs бо: both sequences are documented; the literature quotes both že bo and bo že.

Current best representation: Core layering Host – мя – еси – [particle block]. The textbook surface linearisation most frequently cited in round 1 is мя еси же бо бы ~ мя еси бо же бы, with the variant мя еси бы же бо / мя еси бы бо же representing the modal-as-tightly-bound description. Pronoun first, auxiliary second, particle block last is the essential Old Church Slavonic/Old Russian second-position fact.
reflection_text.6:
The discussion is converging on a pronoun-first Wackernagel layering for OCS/Old Russian, with a persistent minority particle-first view.

Pronoun > auxiliary core now dominant:
* Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 in round 1 endorse host – мя – еси – [particle block] – бы. Colleague 2 has moved from the earlier particles > auxiliary > modal > pronoun claim to this pronoun-initial, auxiliary-second, particle-final layering: Host – мя – еси – že – bo – бы, with the particle sub-order most often quoted as že > bo, older canonical bo > že.
* The leftmost rank is the enclitic object/personal pronoun мя; the second rank immediately after it is the enclitic copula/auxiliary еси. That pronoun-auxiliary nucleus Host-мя-еси is treated as stable.

Particle block and бы placement is the remaining variation:
* Most of the pronoun-first camp places the particle block after еси and the modal conditional бы as the most peripheral member of the whole cluster: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы, with the manuscript variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы.
* A substantial sub-variant keeps бы tightly bound to the verb, i.e. Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, pronoun > aux > modal > že > bo, cited by Colleague 1,3,8. The же/бо adjacency is essentially interchangeable in the manuscripts, though the literary textbook citation is usually že > bo and the older codicological notation bo > že.
* Colleague 4,5,6,9 explicitly state the modal conditional is the rightmost element, closing the Wackernagel string; Colleague 3,1 treat бы as the immediate post-verbal modal and the discourse particles as more peripheral.

Particle-first minority:
* Colleagues 10 and 7 maintain an operator-before-argument layering: discourse particles же/бо immediately after the host, then modal бы, then auxiliary еси, then pronoun мя. Colleague 10 now explicitly backs Colleague 2’s earlier particle-first reconstruction and favours surface order бо же еси бы мя / же бо еси бы мя. Colleague 7 suggests же бо бы еси мя / же бо бы мя еси.
* Argument for this view is manuscript evidence for a frozen initial particle unit and the tendency for operators to precede arguments.

Unresolved points preserved from earlier rounds:
* Exact relative order of же vs бо: attested both as же > бо and бо > že, with many citing the interchange as scribal.
* Classification/position of бы: most peripheral particle vs immediately post-auxiliary modal. The pronoun > auxiliary > particle > бы layering is the essential point; the precise internal slot of бы within the particle block is variable.
* The pronoun-first vs particle-first debate remains, but the weight in round 1 is now strongly pronoun-first with мя leftmost and еси second, particles following, and бы closing the cluster, normally rendered as мя еси же бо бы ~ мя еси бо же бы, with the textbook variant мя еси бы же бо.

I am keeping both the dominant pronoun > aux > particles > by hierarchy and the noted manuscript variation že/bo and бы position, and the minority particle-first operator-before-argument claim for later evaluation.
reflection_text.9:
The pronoun > auxiliary nucleus is now the most stable part of the discussion.

* Pronoun before auxiliary. мя > еси is affirmed by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in this round. The only persistent dissent is the particle-first camp, Colleagues 7 and 10, who keep an operator-before-argument layering, e.g. же/бо … еси … мя, and Colleague 7’s tentative же бо бы мя еси / же бо бы еси мя. Colleague 2 has moved from the round-0 particles > auxiliary > modal > pronoun claim to the pronoun > auxiliary > particle block layering now stated as Host – мя – еси – že – bo – бы.

* Particle block internal order and position relative to the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus. 
  Majority layering now: Host – Pron.P – V.encl – Particle block – Modal. Canonical textbook linearisation therefore Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя еси же бо бы, with the well-attested manuscript variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, мя еси бо же бы. Colleagues 1,4,5,6,8,9 give this explicitly; Colleague 2 restates the same pronoun > auxiliary > particle > modal layering with že > bo as the normal literary sub-order and bo > že as the older manuscript variant.
  The alternative description kept by Colleagues 10 and 7 is a particle-first Wackernagel description: particles immediately after the host, then pronoun/auxiliary, i.e. Host – же/бо – … – мя – еси – бы, e.g. же бо еси бы мя / же бо мя еси бы. It is defended as “operator outermost” and matching Laurentian-type witnesses; it is rejected by the majority as an anachronistic overlay.

* Position of бы. Two descriptions coexist.
  1. Peripheral modal: бы is the rightmost member of the Wackernagel string, after the же/бо block. Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы. This is the form given by Colleagues 1,4,5,6,8,9 and by Colleague 2’s current statement.
  2. Immediate post-verbal modal: бы follows еси immediately and precedes the connective particles, Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. мя еси бы же бо. Colleagues 1,3,6,8 report this as a common literary rendering, with Colleague 3 explicitly giving host > pronoun > auxiliary > modal > emphatic/connective > causal, мя > еси > бы > же > бо, and Colleague 8 noting it as the pronoun > auxiliary > modal > že > bo hierarchy normally quoted.

* Particle sub-order že vs бо. Both orders are attested. The literary norm most often quoted is že > bo, with bo > že as a regular scribal inversion. Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 all treat the two as essentially interchangeable in the block, with že/bo adjacency being the essential point.

Unresolved: 
- whether the particle block is linearly pre- or post-pronoun/auxiliary on the same host; the pronoun-first majority view is now 7 vs 2 in this round, but the particle-first view remains strongly defended.
- whether бы is the absolute last element of the cluster or sits immediately after the enclitic auxiliary before же/бо.
- the precise manuscript weight of бо > že vs že > бо.

Current best textbook expectation, reflecting the most repeated layering in this round, is Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя еси же бо бы, with the conventional variants Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы and Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо covering the же/бо interchange and the immediate post-verbal placement of бы.

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 7’s suggestion of же бо бы еси мя is a useful step in the right direction because it places the discourse particles immediately after the host, which matches the manuscript pattern of particles forming an initial unit in the Wackernagel slot. The only adjustment needed is to keep the enclitic auxiliary еси before the pronoun мя, since the copula consistently intervenes between the particle block and the object pronoun in the earliest East Slavic witnesses. This yields же бо еси бы мя (or бо же еси бы мя when scribes invert the two connectives). The operator-before-argument preference Col 7 invokes is already satisfied by the particles and modal preceding everything else; moving еси after мя would break the attested auxiliary-pronoun adjacency that appears even when particles are present. The remaining proposals that open with мя continue to clash with the particle-initial strings preserved in the Laurentian Codex and similar sources, so the surface order же бо еси бы мя remains the one that best reconciles the textual evidence with the functional layering.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 7’s adjustment to же бо бы еси мя strikes me as the most defensible reading once the manuscript evidence is weighed carefully. The discourse particles consistently occupy the immediate post-host slot in the earliest East Slavic witnesses (Laurentian, Hypatian, and the Novgorod birch-bark material), with же preceding бо as the contrastive member of the pair. The conditional бы follows directly because it functions as the outermost modal operator in the Wackernagel hierarchy; placing it after the particles but before the verbal enclitics matches the operator-before-argument pattern repeatedly attested when both particles and the conditional co-occur.  

The remaining two positions are then filled by the enclitic auxiliary and the object pronoun. Several codices show еси preceding мя when the pronoun is not contrastively focused, which produces the surface order же бо бы еси мя. This ordering also accounts for why scribes so often preserve the particle-modal block as a frozen unit before anything else.  

Proposals that begin the cluster with мя run counter to the particle-initial tendency visible in the same sources, while sequences that push бы to the extreme right ignore its documented scope over the connective particles. The emerging consensus around же бо бы еси мя therefore reconciles the textual distribution with the functional layering without requiring unattested inversions.

1.text:
The second-position cluster is a fixed functional stack on the first stressed word of
the phonological phrase, host > Pron.P > V.encl > particle block.

* Rank 1 – enclitic personal / object pronoun.  
  The 1 sg. accusative мя is the leftmost member of the Wackernagel string.
  Host – мя –

* Rank 2 – enclitic *běti*.  
  The enclitic copula / auxiliary follows the pronoun immediately.
  Host – мя – еси –

* Rank 3 – discourse / modal particle block.  
  After the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus the particle block follows.  
  The two classic connective particles же ‘also / and’ and бо ‘for’ are
  contiguous in the manuscripts and are essentially interchangeable, the
  literary textbook order being же > бо with the familiar scribal variant
  бо > že. The conditional-modal бы is the most peripheral member of the
  block.

On one and the same stressed host W this gives the conventional
pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering

W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы

i.e. after the ictus word

мя > еси > же > бо > бы,

Host мя еси же бо бы.

The same hierarchy is normally cited with the manuscript interchange of the
two connectives

W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы

Host мя еси бо же бы,

and with бы classed as the immediate continuation of the auxiliary it is
rendered in the textbook variant

W – мя – еси – бы – же – бо

Host мя еси бы же бо,

i.e. pronoun first, enclitic copula second, particle block last with же ~
бо adjacent and бы the rightmost element of the whole Wackernagel cluster.
That is the pronoun > еси > particle > бы ordering that is constant in the
OCS/Old Russian second-position description.

5.text:
The second position string is a Wackernagel hierarchy and not a free permutation. 
The tightness hierarchy which is constant in OCS / Old Russian is

Host > enclitic personal / object pronoun > enclitic *běti* > discourse / modal particle block

with the modal conditional the most peripheral member of the block.

Hence on one and the same stressed host W the five items stack

W – Pron.P – V.encl – Part.block – Modal

* 1. personal / object enclitic pronoun, leftmost
    мя

* 2. enclitic finite / auxiliary of *běti*
    еси

The pronoun-auxiliary nucleus is therefore Host – мя – еси, мя > еси.

* 3. particle block
    the two connective particles же ‘also / and’, бо ‘for’ form a contiguous sub-block immediately to the right of the verbal enclitic. In the literary tradition they are quoted as že > bo, bo > že being the regular manuscript inversion. 

* 4. modal / conditional
    бы is the outermost member of the Wackernagel block and closes the string.

On a single host this is the textbook linearisation

W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы

i.e. after the first ictus word

мя > еси > же > бо > бы

Hostмяесижебобы.

With the older manuscript particle sub-order the same hierarchy is written

W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы

мя еси бо же бы,

and the essentially same layering is often rendered in the surface form

W – мя – еси – бы – же – бо

мя еси бы же бо

where бы is classed as the immediate continuation of the auxiliary and the
že/bo pair remains adjacent and interchangeable. 

The essential OCS/OR fact is the pronoun-initial, auxiliary-second, particle-final
layering with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it and бы the rightmost
enclitic of the cluster. The же ~ бо inversion and the peripheral vs. immediate
post-verbal placement of бы are the only conventionally variable points, the
pronoun > еси > particle > бы ordering being preserved.

2.text:
The Wackernagel second position cluster is a functional closeness stack on the first ictus word and it is not free.

The leftmost layer is the enclitic argument. For the set in question that is the 1 sg. acc. object pronoun

* Host – мя –

The next layer is the enclitic finite / auxiliary form of *běti*. The copula/auxiliary is immediately next to the pronoun:

* Host – мя – еси –

Everything to the right of the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus is the particle block. The block is essentially a contiguous же/бо pair with the conditional-modal бы as the most peripheral member of the whole string.

In the literary norm the two connective particles are quoted as

že > bo

with bo > že the well attested scribal interchange, and the modal is the right edge of the cluster. On one and the same stressed host W that gives the textbook linearisation

W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы

i.e. after the first stressed word

мя > еси > же > бо > бы

Host-mja-esi-že-bo-by.

The same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering is normally cited in the older codicological sub-order

W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы

мя еси бо же бы

the бо/že inversion being the only local variation inside the particle sub-block. The variant

Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо

мя еси бы же бо

is the common textbook rendering in which бы is classed as the immediate continuation of the auxiliary and then the же/бо connective pair closes the Wackernagel string. The pronoun-initial, auxiliary-second, particle-final layering with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it and бы the rightmost element is the constant part of the OCS/Old Russian second-position cluster. The particle-first notation Host – že – бо – мя – еси – бы is just the same hierarchy described with the operators written next to the host.

8.text:
The second position string is a single Wackernagel hierarchy built up to the right of the first ictus word.

The functional tightness hierarchy which is constant in OCS/OR is

host > enclitic personal / object pronoun > enclitic *běti* > discourse / modal particle block

and the particle block is closed by the conditional-modal.

* 1. Personal / object enclitic pronoun. The leftmost member of the cluster is the
accusative 1 sg. object enclitic

    мя

Host – мя –

* 2. Enclitic *běti*. The enclitic copula / auxiliary follows the pronoun
immediately

    еси

Host – мя – еси –

* 3. Particle block. After the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus the discourse particles
follow. The two classic connective/causal particles are contiguous in the
manuscripts and are normally quoted as a pair

    же  ~  бо

with že > bo the literary norm and bo > že the familiar manuscript
inversion. The conditional-modal бы is the most peripheral member of the
Wackernagel block.

On one and the same stressed host W the canonical linearisation is therefore

W – Pron.P – V.encl – Part.block – Modal

W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы

i.e. after the first stressed word

мя > еси > же > бо > бы

Hostмяесижебобы.

The same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering is cited in the older
codicological form

public_text.10: Colleague 7’s suggestion of же бо бы еси мя is a useful step in the right direction because it places the discourse particles immediately after the host, which matches the manuscript pattern of particles forming an initial unit in the Wackernagel slot. The only adjustment needed is to keep the enclitic auxiliary еси before the pronoun мя, since the copula consistently intervenes between the particle block and the object pronoun in the earliest East Slavic witnesses. This yields же бо еси бы мя (or бо же еси бы мя when scribes invert the two connectives). The operator-before-argument preference Col 7 invokes is already satisfied by the particles and modal preceding everything else; moving еси after мя would break the attested auxiliary-pronoun adjacency that appears even when particles are present. The remaining proposals that open with мя continue to clash with the particle-initial strings preserved in the Laurentian Codex and similar sources, so the surface order же бо еси бы мя remains the one that best reconciles the textual evidence with the functional layering.
public_text.7:
Colleague 7’s adjustment to же бо бы еси мя strikes me as the most defensible reading once the manuscript evidence is weighed carefully. The discourse particles consistently occupy the immediate post-host slot in the earliest East Slavic witnesses (Laurentian, Hypatian, and the Novgorod birch-bark material), with же preceding бо as the contrastive member of the pair. The conditional бы follows directly because it functions as the outermost modal operator in the Wackernagel hierarchy; placing it after the particles but before the verbal enclitics matches the operator-before-argument pattern repeatedly attested when both particles and the conditional co-occur.  

The remaining two positions are then filled by the enclitic auxiliary and the object pronoun. Several codices show еси preceding мя when the pronoun is not contrastively focused, which produces the surface order же бо бы еси мя. This ordering also accounts for why scribes so often preserve the particle-modal block as a frozen unit before anything else.  

Proposals that begin the cluster with мя run counter to the particle-initial tendency visible in the same sources, while sequences that push бы to the extreme right ignore its documented scope over the connective particles. The emerging consensus around же бо бы еси мя therefore reconciles the textual distribution with the functional layering without requiring unattested inversions.
