reflection_text.2:
The deliberation remains anchored on the Wackernagel second-position cluster for Old Church Slavonic/Old Russian and the linear hierarchy on a single stressed host.

Core stable majority across rounds 2-3, colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9:
* Host is first ictus word; cluster is built to its right by functional tightness.
* Rank 1 most tightly bound: enclitic argument. Leftmost clitic after host is the 1 sg. acc. object pronoun мя. Host – мя –
* Rank 2: enclitic *běti*. The enclitic copula/auxiliary еси follows the pronoun immediately and forms the stable pronoun-auxiliary nucleus Host – мя – еси –; мя > еси is constant, e.g. възлюби мя еси ли.
* Rank 3: discourse / modal particle block to the right of the nucleus. же and бо are contiguous and essentially interchangeable in the manuscript tradition. Literary norm quoted as же > бо with regular older codicological/scribal variant бо > že. The pair is adjacent to the nucleus.
* Rank 4 modal periphery: conditional-modal бы is the most peripheral member of the whole Wackernagel cluster and closes the string to the right of the же/бо pair.

Canonical linearisations cited by the majority:
* Textbook pronoun > auxiliary > particles > modal: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя еси же бо бы.
* Same hierarchy with particle sub-order inversion: Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, мя еси бо же бы.
* Textbook modal-immediate variant: Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, мя еси бы же бо, i.e. бы classed as immediate continuation of the auxiliary before the же/бо pair.

Remaining minority / debate:
* Particle-first / operator-before-argument layering. Colleague 10 and 7 continue to defend discourse particles immediately next to the host. Colleague 10 in round 3 partially converges, accepting еси before мя within a particle-adjacent framing, and cites Hypatian/Laurentian/birch-bark evidence for же бо еси бы мя, бо же еси бы мя, and argues for overall particle > auxiliary > modal > pronoun sequence. Colleague 7 maintains же бо бы еси мя / же бо еси бы мя and stresses particle-modal unit leftmost, бы preceding verbal enclitics, and operator-before-argument preference.
* Majority 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 treat particle-first notations Host-že-bo-mja-esi-by as a re-description of the same hierarchy with operators written next to the host, and explicitly call operator-before-argument surface order anachronistic.

Unresolved points persisting:
* Exact relative placement of бы inside the block: outermost after же/бо vs immediate post-auxiliary before же/бо.
* Exact же vs бо order: literary norm же > бо vs canonical manuscript bo > že; both attested.

Errors/corrections noticed:
* Pronoun-initial view is now dominant; the earlier round 0 particle > auxiliary > modal > pronoun hierarchy is largely abandoned except by 10 and 7.
* Colleague 10’s round 3 adjustment to keep еси before мя acknowledges attested auxiliary-pronoun adjacency even within a particle-initial framing.

My current synthesis remains pronoun-initial layering Host – мя – еси – particle block – бы, with particle block essentially же/бо in either order and бы rightmost. Most commonly cited textbook linearisation is мя еси же бо бы, with equivalent variant мя еси бо же бы and traditional modal-immediate variant мя еси бы же бо. Precise бы position and exact же/бо order remain documented points of scribal variation.
reflection_text.4:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster after the first ictus host remains the core problem. Functional classes are stable: мя = 1sg.acc. object pronoun enclitic, еси = 2sg. enclitic copula/auxiliary of *byti*, бы = conditional/modal particle, же = emphatic/connective particle, бо = causal/explanatory particle.

Majority position rounds 0-3 is pronoun-first layering: host > clitic pronoun > clitic auxiliary > particle block, with бы as most peripheral member of the block. Canonical linearisation
Host – мя – еси – {же/бо} – бы
i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы, with mirror Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы.

Variants within that layering:
* же > бо is textbook literary order, бо > же is older manuscript/codicological order, essentially interchangeable and adjacent.
* бы placement is main intra-pronoun-first disagreement. Most common textbook form puts бы last after connective particles: мя еси же бо бы / мя еси бо же бы. Sub-variant places modal immediately after auxiliary and before connective particles: мя еси бы же бо, i.e. pronoun > auxiliary > modal > же > бо, with же regularly preceding бо. Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 explicitly defend this pronoun-first layering in round 3.
* pronoun > auxiliary order is very stable in this camp: мя leftmost, еси follows immediately. Particle block follows verbal enclitic.

Competing particle-first camp, Colleague 10,7, argues for operator-before-argument layering: particles immediately next to host, then modal, then auxiliary, then pronoun. Colleague 10 round 3 adjusts to keep еси before мя, yielding же бо еси бы мя / бо же еси бы мя, and rejects pronoun-first order as anachronistic. Colleague 7 maintains же бо бы еси мя with же preceding бо as contrastive member and бы following particles before verbal enclitics.

Round 3 shows reinforcement of pronoun-first majority with explicit equivalence claims: Colleague 2 notes particle-first notation Host-že-bo-mja-esi-by is same hierarchy described with operators written next to host. Colleagues 3,4,5,8 stress pronoun > еси > particle > бы layering is essential OCS/OR second-position fact; operator-before-argument surface order бо же еси бы мя defended in round 0 is anachronistic overlay.

Unresolved questions persisting:
* Old Russian specifically vs Old Church Slavonic literary norm: is pronoun-first layering a general Slavonic norm or East Slavic textual reality?
* Classification of бы: modal particle peripheral to whole block vs modal tightly bound immediately after enclitic auxiliary еси.
* Stable же/бо sub-order: же > бо in most textbook citations, бо > же in many manuscript witnesses; both attested.
* Relative order of auxiliary еси vs pronoun мя when particle-first description is adopted.

Current best synthesis from majority: essential OCS/OR layering is pronoun-initial, auxiliary-second, particle-final, with мя leftmost, еси next, же/бо pair next, бы rightmost. Surface forms most quoted are мя еси же бо бы and мя еси бо же бы, with common textbook variant мя еси бы же бо for post-verbal modal position. Particle-first orders remain minority competing interpretation, now partially softened to же бо еси бы мя.
reflection_text.3:
The second-position Wackernagel cluster for бы, же, еси, бо, мя is converging on a pronoun-first, auxiliary-second nucleus with a particle/modal block to the right. The majority core is now stable across rounds 1–3: Host – мя – еси – … with мя as leftmost enclitic and еси immediately following it, the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus мя > еси attested e.g. възлюби мя еси ли. Functional tightness hierarchy retained is W > Pron.P > V.encl > particle block > modal periphery.

Inside the particle block the two discourse particles же and бо are contiguous and essentially interchangeable. Literary norm quoted as же > бо; bo > že is the regular older manuscript / codicological variant. Both sub-orders are accepted as local variation; the essential layering is pronoun > auxiliary > že/бо.

бы remains the main source of variation but is described as rightmost. The majority surface citation is Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы, with the same hierarchy rendered as Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы for the bo > že variant. The textbook variant Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо is treated as the same pronoun-first, auxiliary-second, particle-final layering with бы classed as the immediate continuation of the verbal enclitic before the že/бо pair, or as the outermost modal of the block.

Minority positions persist:
* Colleague 10 maintains a particle-initial/operator-before-argument analysis, now refined to же бо еси бы мя / бо же еси бы мя, arguing Laurentian/birch-bark evidence for particles immediately after host and attested еси-mя adjacency, while still denying a pronoun-first nucleus and keeping the overall particle > auxiliary > modal > pronoun sequence. The pronoun-first strings are still claimed to contradict the particle-outermost strings in the same witnesses.
* Colleague 7 maintains же бо бы еси мя, arguing a particle-modal operator unit же бо бы sits immediately post-host and that еси precedes мя only after the operator block is fixed.

No new manuscript evidence has overturned the pronoun-first nucleus. Colleague 10’s concession on еси-mя adjacency narrows his minority position but does not merge it with the majority.

Unresolved questions remaining:
* Canonical sub-order of же vs бо for the period, же > бо vs bo > že, and whether inversion is scribal variation.
* Canonical placement of бы: immediately post-auxiliary as modal continuation vs most peripheral member after the že/бо pair.
* Reconciling particle-first notations Host-že-bo-mja-esi-by with the linear pronoun-first description; majority treats it as a reclassification of the same hierarchy, minority treats it as substantive.

Current working hypothesis: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with acknowledged variants Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы and Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, all expressing pronoun > auxiliary > particle/modal layering with že/бо freely interchanged and бы rightmost, with particle-first proposals remaining an isolated minority.
reflection_text.6:
The discussion stays on Wackernagel second-position cluster internal tightness and pronoun-first vs particle-first layering.

Stable majority core, reiterated by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 3:
* Host > enclitic argument > enclitic *běti* > particle block > modal periphery.
* Rank 1 most tightly bound is the 1 sg. acc. object enclitic pronoun мя, leftmost after the host: W – мя –
* Rank 2 is enclitic *běti* еси immediately after the pronoun. The pronoun-auxiliary nucleus мя > еси is treated as invariant, e.g. *възлюби мя еси ли*.
* Rank 3 is the discourse particle block to the right of the nucleus. же ‘also/and’ and бо ‘for’ are contiguous and essentially interchangeable in manuscripts; literary textbook norm quoted as же > бо with the regular older codicological/scribal variant бо > že.
* Rank 4 modal periphery: conditional-modal бы is the most peripheral member of the whole Wackernagel string, closing the cluster to the right of the же/бо pair.

Canonical linearisation given repeatedly:
W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы   i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы
Host мя еси же бо бы.
Manuscript sub-order variant:
W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы   мя еси бо же бы
Textbook modal-immediate variant:
W – мя – еси – бы – же – бо   мя еси бы же бо
The invariant described as pronoun-first, еси-second, же/бо adjacent interchangeable, бы rightmost.

Particle-first minority:
* Colleague 7 holds же бо бы еси мя, arguing discourse particles form a single operator unit immediately post-host, бы scopes over connectives and precedes verbal enclitics, and еси precedes мя once the operator block is fixed. Cites Laurentian/Hypatian/earliest East Slavic witnesses for particle-initial tendency and operator-before-argument layering.
* Colleague 10 now moves from round-0 же бо бы еси мя toward a compromise aligning with particle-initial evidence but preserving auxiliary-pronoun adjacency: же бо еси бы мя / бо же еси бы мя. Argument: particles sit immediately after host in Laurentian/birch-bark evidence; attested adjacency еси…мя in Hypatian Codex favors copula intervening between particle/modal unit and accusative pronoun; reversing auxiliary-pronoun order would be unattested when particles are clause-initial. Still rejects pronoun-first nucleus мя > еси as opening of the cluster.

Unresolved tensions preserved:
* Exact relative order of же vs бо: attested both же > бо and бо > že; treated as scribal interchange.
* Classification/position of бы: majority keeps бы as rightmost peripheral element closing the cluster; sub-variant places бы immediately after еси before же/бо pair: мя еси бы же бо.
* Pronoun-first vs particle-first debate persists. Weight in rounds 1-3 is strongly pronoun-initial with мя leftmost and еси second, particles following, бы closing. Particle-first view is defended on manuscript surface strings with particles as leftmost Wackernagel material and operator-before-argument preference, with Colleague 10 partially converging toward a hybrid же бо еси бы мя and Colleague 7 holding же бо бы еси мя.

Current belief keeps the dominant pronoun > auxiliary > particles > бы hierarchy with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it, же/бо adjacent interchangeable, бы rightmost, while retaining the minority particle-initial operator-before-argument claim and the noted manuscript variation for later evaluation.
reflection_text.5:
The discussion remains polarised pronoun-first vs particle-first surface notation, but round 3 again heavily reinforces the pronoun-first layering.

Working hypothesis retained: Host – Pron.P – V.encl – particle block – modal, with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it, and бы the most peripheral member of the cluster. The core nucleus Host – мя – еси is now repeatedly affirmed by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 3.

Evidence cited in round 3:
* Functional tightness = left-to-right: enclitic personal/object pronoun most tightly bound, enclitic *běti* next, discourse particles next, conditional modal most peripheral.
* Pronoun-auxiliary nucleus мя > еси is stable, e.g. *възлюби мя еси ли*.
* The two connective particles же and бо form a contiguous essentially interchangeable sub-block. Literary norm quoted as že > bo; manuscript/codicological norm bo > že. Both treated as scribal variants of same adjacency.
* бы is described as the right-most element of the Wackernagel string. Two conventional renderings coexist:
  – textbook peripheral: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы / Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы
  – textbook post-auxiliary modal: Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. мя еси бы же бо, where бы is classed as immediate continuation of the auxiliary before the že/bo pair.

Competing view persisting:
* Colleague 10 continues particle-initial / operator-before-argument claim but in round 3 partially concedes auxiliary-pronoun order, moving еси before мя, yielding же бо еси бы мя, or бо же еси бы мя. Argument cites Laurentian/Hypatian particle immediacy and operator-before-argument preference, and claims pronoun-first strings contradict particle-outermost strings in witnesses.
* Colleague 7 maintains particle-initial бо/же-first order, бо, же, бы, мя, еси / же бо бы еси мя, citing Laurentian/Hypatian particle-initial tendency. This view is now isolated.

Changes/notices round 3:
* Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 all converge on the same canonical linearisation: W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with manuscript variant W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, and the closely related surface variant W – мя – еси – бы – же – бо.
* Colleague 2 explicitly reframes particle-first notation Host – že – бо – мя – еси – бы as same hierarchy described with operators written next to host, not a contradictory ordering.
* No new manuscript citations beyond Laurentian/Hypatian/Lavra birch-bark; debate remains interpretive about classification of бы and linearisation of же/бо.
* Colleague 10’s refinement to же бо еси бы мя keeps particles leftmost but accepts еси > мя adjacency, reducing but not eliminating the conflict with pronoun-first nucleus.

Unresolved points still open:
* Же vs бо sub-order: canonical literary že > bo vs manuscript bo > že.
* Exact rank of бы relative to же/бо: most peripheral after particle pair vs immediately post-auxiliary before же/бо. Both мя еси же бо бы and мя еси бы же бо are presented as conventional variants of same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering.

Current belief: canonical OCS/Old Russian second-position order for the set is pronoun first, auxiliary second, then the že/bo pair, then бы last: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with manuscript variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, and closely related surface variant Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо. The essential layering pronoun > еси > particles > бы is retained, with že/bo interchange and бы periphery as remaining variable. Particle-first surface notation is a descriptive reclassification, not a linear contradiction, and remains a minority view against the attested pronoun-auxiliary nucleus мя > еси.
reflection_text.1:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster is now described by a stable majority as a functional tightness stack Host > enclitic argument > enclitic *běti* > discourse/modal particle block with the conditional-modal most peripheral. The invariant core asserted by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 is the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus мя > еси, leftmost after the first ictus word, attested e.g. *възлюби мя еси ли*. 

Rank 1 most tightly bound: 1 sg. acc. object enclitic мя, Host – мя – .
Rank 2: enclitic copula/auxiliary еси, Host – мя – еси – . Pronoun > auxiliary is stable.
Rank 3: discourse particle block to the right of the nucleus. The two classic connectives же ‘also/and’ and бо ‘for’ are contiguous and essentially interchangeable in the manuscripts. Literary textbook norm is quoted as же > бо with the regular older codicological/scribal variant бо > že.
Rank 4 most peripheral: conditional-modal бы closes the whole Wackernagel string to the right of the že/bo pair.

Canonical literary linearisation after the host is therefore

Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы
i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы
Host мя еси же бо бы.

The same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering is cited with the manuscript particle sub-order

Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бо
Host мя еси бо же бы

and with бы classed as the immediate continuation of the verbal enclitic the textbook surface rendering

Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо
Host мя еси бы же бо

Particle-initial minority persists.
Colleague 7 maintains an operator-before-argument reading and defends a leftmost particle-modal unit, e.g. же бо бы еси мя, arguing же бо бы forms a single operator unit routinely placed immediately after the host in Laurentian/Hypatian/Novgorod/birch-bark material and that бы scopes over the connectives before the verbal enclitics. Placing еси before мя is then said to respect attested auxiliary-pronoun adjacency once the operator block is fixed.

Colleague 10 now aligns partially with particle-initial evidence but keeps auxiliary-pronoun adjacency. He notes Laurentian and birch-bark evidence that discourse particles sit immediately after the host, favours же бо еси бы мя or бо же еси бы мя over же бо бы еси мя on the basis of Hypatian-type adjacency where the copula intervenes between the outer particle-modal block and the accusative pronoun, and argues the overall sequence is particle > auxiliary > modal > pronoun, i.e. же бо еси бы мя / бо же еси бы мя. W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы  /  W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы
i.e. after the host мя > еси > же > бо > бы, with the že/bo swap as the only local variation.

Textbook variant widely accepted:
W – мя – еси – бы – же – бо
i.e. мя еси бы же бо, where бы is classed as the immediate continuation of the auxiliary and the že~bo pair closes the cluster. This is treated as the same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering with a descriptive re-classification of бы as tightly bound modal.

Divergence that persists:
* Position of бы inside the block: outermost modal after že/bo vs immediate post-auxiliary modal. Manuscript practice shows both; both are now accepted as conventional variants of the same pronoun-first, auxiliary-second, particle-final layering.
* Order of же vs бо: both sequences are documented; no single canonical order can be imposed without noting the interchangeable manuscript practice.
* Particle-first minority: Colleague 10 and Colleague 7 continue to argue for an operator-initial surface order with discourse particles immediately after the host, e.g. же бо еси бы мя / же бо бы еси мя, invoking Laurentian, Hypatian, Novgorod birch-bark. Colleague 10 now adjusts to auxiliary before pronoun, же бо еси бы мя, invoking particle-initial strings. Colleague 7 maintains бо/же > бы > мя > еси. This minority is opposed by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 who explicitly reject particle-first as an anachronistic overlay and note that the particle-first notation is the same hierarchy described with different classification.

Changes in belief:
* Pronoun-first vs particle-first split is now strongly resolved in favour of pronoun-first. Colleague 2’s earlier particle-first claim is retracted and now endorses Host – мя – еси – …
* The earlier working hypothesis Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо remains a well-attested variant, but the default surface citation now tends to Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы with бы outermost.

Unresolved:
* Exact rank of бы relative to же/бо: outermost modal vs immediate post-verbal modal. Both are documented and both are now accepted as conventional variants.
* Fixed order of же vs бо: both attested; no single canonical order can be imposed without noting the interchangeable manuscript practice.

Essential fact retained: pronoun first, еси second, particle block last, бы rightmost. The linear order мя еси [же/бо] бы is the constant part; že~bo adjacency and бы periphery are the invariant features.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation remains anchored on Wackernagel second-position cluster for Old Church Slavonic/Old Russian on a single stressed host.

Core stable majority across rounds 2-4, colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9:
* Host is first ictus word; cluster built to its right by functional tightness.
* Rank 1 most tightly bound: enclitic argument. Leftmost clitic after host is the 1 sg. acc. object pronoun мя. Host – мя –
* Rank 2: enclitic *běti*. The enclitic copula/auxiliary еси follows the pronoun immediately and forms stable pronoun-auxiliary nucleus Host – мя – еси –; мя > еси is constant, e.g. възлюби мя еси ли.
* Rank 3: discourse particle block to right of nucleus. же and бо are contiguous and essentially interchangeable in manuscript tradition. Literary norm quoted as же > бо with regular older codicological/scribal variant бо > že. Pair is adjacent to nucleus.
* Rank 4 modal periphery: conditional-modal бы is most peripheral member and closes string to right of же/бо pair.

Canonical linearisations cited by majority in round 4:
* Textbook pronoun > auxiliary > particles > modal: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя еси же бо бы.
* Same hierarchy with particle sub-order inversion: Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, мя еси бо же бы.
* Textbook modal-immediate variant: Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, мя еси бы же бо, i.e. бы classed as immediate continuation of auxiliary before же/бо pair.

Round 4 restatement shows no new shift in majority; 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 explicitly reiterate pronoun-first, еси second, že~bo adjacent interchangeable, бы rightmost, and treat particle-first surface notations Host-že-bo-...-мя-...-еси-...-бы as re-description with operators written next to host, not overturning linear мя > еси order.

Minority / debate persists:
* Particle-first / operator-before-argument layering. Colleague 10 continues to defend discourse operators form immediate post-host unit: attested copula-pronoun adjacency once unit fixed favors же бо еси бы мя or бо же еси бы мя over же бо бы еси мя. Claims majority strings contradict particle-outermost examples preserved in earliest East Slavic material; treats же and бо as leftmost Wackernagel material. Accepts еси before мя within particle-adjacent framing, cites Hypatian/Laurentian/birch-bark evidence for же бо еси бы мя, бо же еси бы мя.
* Colleague 7 maintains же бо бы еси мя / же бо еси бы мя, stresses particle-modal unit leftmost, бы preceding verbal enclitics, and operator-before-argument preference.

Unresolved points persisting:
* Exact relative placement of бы: outermost after же/бо vs immediate post-auxiliary before же/бо.
* Exact же vs бо order: literary norm же > бо vs canonical manuscript бо > že; both attested.

Errors/corrections noticed:
* Pronoun-initial view is now dominant; earlier round 0 particle > auxiliary > modal > pronoun hierarchy largely abandoned except by 10 and 7.
* Colleague 10’s round 3-4 adjustment to keep еси before мя acknowledges attested auxiliary-pronoun adjacency even within particle-initial framing.

Current synthesis remains pronoun-initial layering Host – мя – еси – particle block – бы, with particle block essentially же/бо in either order and бы rightmost. Most commonly cited textbook linearisation is мя еси же бо бы, with equivalent variant мя еси бо же бы and traditional modal-immediate variant мя еси бы же бо. Precise бы position and exact же/бо order remain documented points of scribal variation.

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains polarised pronoun-first vs particle-first surface notation, with a stable majority and a persistent minority in round 4.

Working hypothesis retained: Host – Pron.P – V.encl – particle block – modal periphery, with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it, and бы the most peripheral member of the cluster. The core nucleus Host – мя – еси is again repeatedly affirmed by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 4 as invariant, e.g. *възлюби мя еси ли*.

Evidence reiterated in round 4:
* Functional tightness = left-to-right: enclitic personal/object pronoun most tightly bound, enclitic *běti* next, discourse particles next, conditional modal most peripheral.
* Pronoun–auxiliary nucleus мя > еси is stable.
* The two connective particles же and бо form a contiguous essentially interchangeable sub-block. Literary norm quoted as že > bo; manuscript/codicological norm bo > že. Both treated as scribal variants of same adjacency.
* бы is described as right-most element of the Wackernagel string. Two conventional renderings coexist:
  – textbook peripheral: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы / Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы
  – textbook post-auxiliary modal: Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. мя еси бы же бо, where бы is classed as immediate continuation of the auxiliary before the že/bo pair.

Public round 4 positions:
* Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 converge on the same canonical linearisation: W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with manuscript variant W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, and the closely related surface variant W – мя – еси – бы – же – бо. They explicitly state particle-first surface notations Host-že-bo-...-мя-...-еси-...-бы are a re-description of the same hierarchy with operators written next to the host and do not overturn linear мя > еси order on a single host.
* Colleague 10 persists with particle-first synthesis aligned to Laurentian/Hypatian strings, now refining to же бо еси бы мя / бо же еси бы мя, claiming operator-before-argument preference and that copula regularly intervenes between outer particle-modal block and accusative pronoun. Maintains majority strings мя еси же бо бы contradict particle-outermost examples, and argues particle > auxiliary/modal > pronoun sequence.
* Colleague 7 maintains particle-initial бо/же-first order, же бо бы еси мя / бо же бы мя еси, citing Laurentian/Hypatian particle immediacy. Now isolated.

Changes/notices round 4:
* No new manuscript citations beyond Laurentian/Hypatian/Lavra birch-bark; debate remains interpretive about classification of бы and linearisation of же/бо.
* Majority explicitly frames particle-first notation as descriptive reclassification, not a linear contradiction, reinforcing the pronoun > auxiliary > particle > бы layering.
* Colleague 10’s refinement keeps particles leftmost but now places еси before мя in the surface string, reducing but not eliminating conflict with pronoun-first nucleus.

Unresolved points still open:
* Же vs бо sub-order: canonical literary že > bo vs manuscript bo > že.
* Exact rank of бы relative to же/бо: most peripheral after particle pair vs immediately post-auxiliary before же/бо. Both мя еси же бо бы and мя еси бы же бо are presented as conventional variants of same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering.
* Fundamental disagreement on whether the attested second-position order on one host is pronoun-initial or particle-initial; majority treats particle-first as notation, minority treats it as linear fact.

Current belief: canonical OCS/Old Russian second-position order for the set is pronoun first, auxiliary second, then the že/bo pair, then бы last: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with manuscript variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, and closely related surface variant Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо. Essential layering pronoun > еси > particles > бы is retained, with že/bo interchange and бы periphery as remaining variable. Particle-first surface notation remains a minority view against the attested pronoun-auxiliary nucleus мя > еси.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The second-position Wackernagel cluster for бы, же, еси, бо, мя is converging on a pronoun-first, auxiliary-second nucleus with a particle/modal block to the right. The majority core is now stable across rounds 1-4: Host – мя – еси – … with мя as leftmost enclitic and еси immediately following it, the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus мя > еси attested e.g. възлюби мя еси ли. Functional tightness hierarchy retained is Host > Pron.P > V.encl > particle block > modal periphery.

Inside the particle block the two discourse particles же and бо are contiguous and essentially interchangeable. Literary norm quoted as же > бо; бо > že is the regular older manuscript / codicological variant. Both sub-orders are accepted as local variation; essential layering is pronoun > auxiliary > že/бо.

бы remains the main source of variation but is described as rightmost / most peripheral. Majority surface citation is Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы, with same hierarchy rendered as Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы for the бо > že variant. The textbook variant Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо is treated as same pronoun-first, auxiliary-second, particle-final layering with бы classed as immediate continuation of the verbal enclitic before the že/бо pair, or as outermost modal of the block.

Round 4 public: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 explicitly restate the tightness stack Host > enclitic argument > enclitic běti > discourse particle block > modal periphery, with Rank1 мя, Rank2 мя–еси nucleus, Rank3 же~бо interchangeable block, Rank4 бы rightmost. They explicitly identify particle-first surface notations Host-že-bo-…-мя-…-еси-…-бы as a re-description of the same hierarchy with operators written next to the host and not overturning the linear мя > еси order on a single host.

Minority positions persist:
* Colleague 10 maintains a particle-initial/operator-before-argument analysis, now refined to же бо еси бы мя / бо же еси бы мя, arguing Laurentian/Hypatian strings where discourse operators form immediate post-host unit and copula regularly intervenes between outer particle-modal block and accusative pronoun. He still denies a pronoun-first nucleus and keeps overall particle > auxiliary > modal > pronoun sequence, claiming majority strings contradict particle-outermost examples.
* Colleague 7 maintains же бо бы еси мя as best fit to Laurentian/Hypatian, operator unit же бо + scope-marking бы placed immediately after host before verbal/pronominal material, auxiliary and accusative pronoun forming tight inner pair once operator block fixed. He now notes compatibility with Colleague 10’s же бо еси бы мя surface adjustment and continues to exclude any pronoun-auxiliary nucleus.

No new manuscript evidence has overturned the pronoun-first nucleus. Colleague 10’s concession on еси-мя adjacency narrows his minority position but does not merge it with the majority.

Unresolved questions remaining:
* Canonical sub-order of же vs бо for the period, же > бо vs бо > že, and whether inversion is scribal variation.
* Canonical placement of бы: immediately post-auxiliary as modal continuation vs most peripheral member after the že/бо pair.
* Reconciling particle-first notations Host-že-bo-mja-esi-by with linear pronoun-first description; majority treats it as reclassification of same hierarchy, minority treats it as substantive.

Current working hypothesis: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with acknowledged variants Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы and Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, all expressing pronoun > auxiliary > particle/modal layering with že/бо freely interchanged and бы rightmost, with particle-first proposals remaining an isolated minority.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Wackernagel second-position cluster remains the core problem. Functional classes are stable: мя = 1sg.acc. object pronoun enclitic, еси = 2sg. enclitic copula/auxiliary of *běti*, бы = conditional/modal particle, же = emphatic/connective particle, бо = causal/explanatory particle.

Round 4 consensus majority: 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 are now verbatim convergent on a tightness stack on one stressed host:
Host > enclitic argument > enclitic *běti* > discourse particle block > modal periphery.

Rank 1 most tightly bound: enclitic object pronoun
W – мя –

Rank 2: enclitic *běti*. The pronoun–auxiliary nucleus мя > еси is invariant core, e.g. възлюби мя еси ли.

Rank 3: discourse particle block to the right of the nucleus. же ‘also/and’ and бо ‘for’ are contiguous and essentially interchangeable. Literary norm quoted as же > бо with regular older codicological/scribal inversion бо > že.

Rank 4 most peripheral: conditional-modal бы closes the whole Wackernagel string to the right of the že/bo pair.

Canonical literary linearisation after ictus:
W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы
i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы  Host мя еси же бо бы.

Same layering cited with manuscript sub-order inversion
W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы  Host мя еси бо же бы
and with бы classed as immediate continuation of the verbal enclitic in textbook surface rendering
W – мя – еси – бы – же – бо  Host мя еси бы же бо.

The invariant OCS/Old Russian fact in this camp is pronoun-first, еси second, že ~ бо adjacent and interchangeable, бы rightmost. The particle-first surface notations Host-že-bo-...-мя-...-еси-...-бы are described as the same hierarchy re-described with operators written next to the host and do not overturn the linear мя > еси order on a single host.

Minority particle-first camp persists:
Colleague 10 maintains operator-before-argument preference, defends же бо еси бы мя / бо же еси бы мя as coherent with Laurentian/Hypatian strings, claims discourse operators form immediate post-host unit, copula intervenes between outer particle-modal block and accusative pronoun. Rejects unattested pronoun-auxiliary nucleus. Variability left on же ~ бо internal order and placement of бы immediately after auxiliary vs right edge of particle sub-block.
Colleague 7 maintains же бо бы еси мя as best fit for Laurentian/Hypatian, operator unit же бо plus scope-marking бы immediately after host before verbal/pronominal material, with auxiliary and accusative forming tight inner pair. Accepts minor surface adjustment же бо еси бы мя proposed by Colleague 10, preserving particle > auxiliary/modal > pronoun layering.

Unresolved questions persisting:
* Old Russian specifically vs Old Church Slavonic literary norm: is pronoun-first layering a general Slavonic norm or East Slavic textual reality?
* Classification of бы: modal particle peripheral to whole block vs modal tightly bound immediately after enclitic auxiliary еси.
* Stable же/бо sub-order: же > бо in most textbook citations, бо > že in many manuscript witnesses; both attested and treated as interchangeable locally.
* Relative order of auxiliary еси vs pronoun мя when particle-first description is adopted: Colleague 10 now keeps еси before мя, Colleague 7 keeps еси last.

No new manuscript evidence introduced in round 4; the round is reinforcement of pronoun-first majority with explicit equivalence claims and continuation of particle-first minority with slight softening to же бо еси бы мя.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation remains centred on Wackernagel second-position internal tightness and the pronoun-first vs particle-first layering debate.

Stable majority core, reiterated by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 4:
* Host > enclitic argument > enclitic *běti* > discourse particle block > modal periphery.
* Rank 1 most tightly bound is the 1 sg.acc. object enclitic pronoun мя, leftmost after the host: W – мя –
* Rank 2 is enclitic *běti* еси immediately after the pronoun. The pronoun-auxiliary nucleus мя > еси is treated as invariant, e.g. *възлюби мя еси ли*.
* Rank 3 is the discourse particle block to the right of the nucleus. же ‘also/and’ and бо ‘for’ are contiguous and essentially interchangeable in manuscripts; literary textbook norm quoted as же > бо with the regular older codicological/scribal variant бо > že.
* Rank 4 modal periphery: conditional-modal бы is the most peripheral member of the whole Wackernagel string, closing the cluster to the right of the же/бо pair.

Canonical linearisation given repeatedly:
W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы
Host мя еси же бо бы.
Manuscript sub-order variant:
W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы i.e. мя еси бо же бы
Textbook modal-immediate variant:
W – мя – еси – бы – же – бо i.e. мя еси бы же бо
The invariant described as pronoun-first, еси-second, же/бо adjacent interchangeable, бы rightmost.

Particle-first minority persists:
* Colleague 7 holds же бо бы еси мя as best aligning with Laurentian/Hypatian strings where the discourse-operator unit же бо plus scope-marking бы is placed immediately after the host before verbal/pronominal material. Now notes compatibility with the minor surface adjustment же бо еси бы мя, arguing both preserve leftmost particle placement and exclude a pronoun-auxiliary nucleus.
* Colleague 10 maintains particle-first synthesis is most coherent with Laurentian/Hypatian/birch-bark evidence where discourse operators form an immediate post-host unit. Argues attested copula-pronoun adjacency once that unit is fixed favours же бо еси бы мя / бо же еси бы мя over же бо бы еси мя, because the copula regularly intervenes between the outer particle-modal block and the accusative pronoun. Rejects the pronoun-first nucleus мя > еси as opening the cluster and claims majority strings мя еси же бо бы contradict particle-outermost examples in earliest East Slavic material. Remaining variability is internal же ~ бо order and placement of бы immediately after auxiliary vs right edge of particle sub-block.

Unresolved tensions preserved:
* Exact relative order of же vs бо: attested both же > бо and бо > že; treated as scribal interchange.
* Classification/position of бы: majority keeps бы as rightmost peripheral element closing the cluster; sub-variant places бы immediately after еси before же/бо pair: мя еси бы же бо.
* Pronoun-first vs particle-first debate persists. Weight in rounds 1-4 is strongly pronoun-initial with мя leftmost and еси second, particles following, бы closing. Particle-first view is defended on manuscript surface strings with particles as leftmost Wackernagel material and operator-before-argument layering, with Colleague 10 partially converging toward hybrid же бо еси бы мя and Colleague 7 holding же бо бы еси мя.

Current belief keeps the dominant pronoun > auxiliary > particles > бы hierarchy with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it, же/бо adjacent interchangeable, бы rightmost, while retaining the minority particle-initial operator-before-argument claim and the noted manuscript variation for later evaluation.

reflection_text.1:
The Wackernagel second-position stack for Old Russian/OCS on one stressed host is now described by a stable majority of Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 as a functional tightness stack Host > enclitic argument > enclitic *běti* > discourse particle block > modal periphery, with the conditional-modal most peripheral.

Invariant core asserted by the majority:
* Rank 1 most tightly bound: enclitic object pronoun. Host – мя –
* Rank 2: enclitic copula/auxiliary *běti*. Pronoun–auxiliary nucleus мя > еси is stable, e.g. *възлюби мя еси ли*. Host – мя – еси –
* Rank 3: discourse particle sub-block to the right of the nucleus. же ‘also/and’ and бо ‘for’ are contiguous and essentially interchangeable in manuscripts. Literary norm quoted as же > бо with regular older codicological/scribal variant бо > že.
* Rank 4 most peripheral: conditional-modal бы closes the whole Wackernagel string to the right of the že/bo pair.

Canonical literary linearisation after the host is therefore
Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы
i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы
Host мя еси же бо бы.

The same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering is cited with the manuscript particle sub-order inversion
Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы
Host мя еси бо же бы,
and descriptively with бы classed as the immediate continuation of the verbal enclitic
Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо
Host мя еси бы же бо.

The invariant part is pronoun-first, еси second, the že ~ бо pair adjacent and interchangeable, and бы rightmost. Particle-first surface notations Host-že-bo-…-мя-…-еси-…-бы are treated by the majority as the same hierarchy described with operators written next to the host and not overturning the linear мя > еси order on a single host.

Particle-initial minority persists.
Colleague 7 maintains an operator-before-argument reading and defends a leftmost particle-modal unit, e.g. же бо бы еси мя, arguing же бо бы forms a single operator unit routinely placed immediately after the host in Laurentian/Hypatian/Novgorod/birch-bark material and that бы scopes over the connectives before the verbal enclitics. Placing еси before мя is then said to respect attested auxiliary-pronoun adjacency once the operator block is fixed.

Colleague 10 now aligns partially with particle-initial evidence but keeps auxiliary-pronoun adjacency. He still states that pronoun-first strings contradict particle-outermost strings preserved in the same witnesses and treats the pronoun-first notation as a descriptive reclassification.

* exact relative rank of бы with respect to же/бо – most peripheral after the že/bo pair vs immediate post-auxiliary before the že/bo pair;
* exact же ~ бо sub-order, both variants being scribally common;

The essential disagreement is therefore pronoun-initial, auxiliary-second, particle-final with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it and бы rightmost, versus an operator-first description with the же/бо particle-modal unit leftmost and the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus relocated to the right of it. The majority convergence on мя > еси > [же/бо] > бы with же ~ бо interchangeable remains the working hierarchy, with the particle-initial reading still contested.

reflection_text.8:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster is now strongly resolved as pronoun-initial on the first stressed host: Host > enclitic personal/object pronoun > enclitic *běti* > particle block, with the conditional/modal closing the string to the right.

Common ground after round 4:
* Rank 1 leftmost is the enclitic argument. For the set in question that is мя. Host – мя –
* Rank 2 immediately follows the pronoun is the enclitic copula/auxiliary еси. The pronoun-auxiliary nucleus мя > еси is stable, e.g. *възлюби мя еси ли*. Host – мя – еси –
* Rank 3 is the discourse/modal particle block to the right of the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus. The two classic connectives же and бо are contiguous and essentially interchangeable; literary norm is quoted as же > bo with bo > že the regular older manuscript/scribal inversion.
* Rank 4 is modal periphery. The conditional-modal бы is the most peripheral member of the whole Wackernagel string and closes the cluster to the right of the že/bo pair.

Canonical linearisation most frequently cited:
W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы  /  W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы
i.e. after the host мя > еси > же > бо > бы, with the že/bo swap as the only local variation.

Textbook variant widely accepted:
W – мя – еси – бы – же – бо
i.e. мя еси бы же бо, where бы is classed as the immediate continuation of the auxiliary and the že~bo pair closes the cluster. This is treated as the same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering with a descriptive re-classification of бы as tightly bound modal.

Divergence that persists:
* Position of бы inside the block: outermost modal after že/bo vs immediate post-auxiliary modal. Manuscript practice shows both; both are now accepted as conventional variants of the same pronoun-first, auxiliary-second, particle-final layering.
* Order of же vs бо: both sequences are documented; no single canonical order can be imposed without noting the interchangeable manuscript practice.
* Particle-first minority: Colleague 10 and Colleague 7 continue to argue for an operator-initial surface order with discourse particles immediately after the host, e.g. же бо еси бы мя / же бо бы еси мя, invoking Laurentian, Hypatian, Novgorod birch-bark. Colleague 10 now adjusts to auxiliary before pronoun, же бо еси бы мя, invoking particle-initial strings. Colleague 7 maintains бо/же > бы > мя > еси. This minority is opposed by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 who explicitly reject particle-first as an anachronistic overlay and note that the particle-first notation is the same hierarchy described with different classification.

Changes in belief:
* Pronoun-first vs particle-first split is now strongly resolved in favour of pronoun-first. Colleague 2’s earlier particle-first claim is retracted and now endorses Host – мя – еси – …
* The earlier working hypothesis Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо remains a well-attested variant, but the default surface citation now tends to Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы with бы outermost.

Unresolved:
* Exact rank of бы relative to же/бо: outermost modal vs immediate post-verbal modal. Both are documented and both are now accepted as conventional variants.
* Fixed order of же vs бо: both attested; no single canonical order can be imposed without noting the interchangeable manuscript practice.

Essential fact retained: pronoun first, еси second, particle block last, бы rightmost. The linear order мя еси [же/бо] бы is the constant part; že~bo adjacency and бы periphery are the invariant features.
reflection_text.2:
The deliberation remains anchored on Wackernagel second-position cluster for Old Church Slavonic/Old Russian on a single stressed host.

Core stable majority across rounds 2-4, colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9:
* Host is first ictus word; cluster built to its right by functional tightness.
* Rank 1 most tightly bound: enclitic argument. Leftmost clitic after host is the 1 sg. acc. object pronoun мя. Host – мя –
* Rank 2: enclitic *běti*. The enclitic copula/auxiliary еси follows the pronoun immediately and forms stable pronoun-auxiliary nucleus Host – мя – еси –; мя > еси is constant, e.g. възлюби мя еси ли.
* Rank 3: discourse particle block to right of nucleus. же and бо are contiguous and essentially interchangeable in manuscript tradition. Literary norm quoted as же > бо with regular older codicological/scribal variant бо > že. Pair is adjacent to nucleus.
* Rank 4 modal periphery: conditional-modal бы is most peripheral member and closes string to right of же/бо pair.

Canonical linearisations cited by majority in round 4:
* Textbook pronoun > auxiliary > particles > modal: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя еси же бо бы.
* Same hierarchy with particle sub-order inversion: Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, мя еси бо же бы.
* Textbook modal-immediate variant: Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, мя еси бы же бо, i.e. бы classed as immediate continuation of auxiliary before же/бо pair.

Round 4 restatement shows no new shift in majority; 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 explicitly reiterate pronoun-first, еси second, že~bo adjacent interchangeable, бы rightmost, and treat particle-first surface notations Host-že-bo-...-мя-...-еси-...-бы as re-description with operators written next to host, not overturning linear мя > еси order.

Minority / debate persists:
* Particle-first / operator-before-argument layering. Colleague 10 continues to defend discourse operators form immediate post-host unit: attested copula-pronoun adjacency once unit fixed favors же бо еси бы мя or бо же еси бы мя over же бо бы еси мя. Claims majority strings contradict particle-outermost examples preserved in earliest East Slavic material; treats же and бо as leftmost Wackernagel material. Accepts еси before мя within particle-adjacent framing, cites Hypatian/Laurentian/birch-bark evidence for же бо еси бы мя, бо же еси бы мя.
* Colleague 7 maintains же бо бы еси мя / же бо еси бы мя, stresses particle-modal unit leftmost, бы preceding verbal enclitics, and operator-before-argument preference.

Unresolved points persisting:
* Exact relative placement of бы: outermost after же/бо vs immediate post-auxiliary before же/бо.
* Exact же vs бо order: literary norm же > бо vs canonical manuscript бо > že; both attested.

Errors/corrections noticed:
* Pronoun-initial view is now dominant; earlier round 0 particle > auxiliary > modal > pronoun hierarchy largely abandoned except by 10 and 7.
* Colleague 10’s round 3-4 adjustment to keep еси before мя acknowledges attested auxiliary-pronoun adjacency even within particle-initial framing.

Current synthesis remains pronoun-initial layering Host – мя – еси – particle block – бы, with particle block essentially же/бо in either order and бы rightmost. Most commonly cited textbook linearisation is мя еси же бо бы, with equivalent variant мя еси бо же бы and traditional modal-immediate variant мя еси бы же бо. Precise бы position and exact же/бо order remain documented points of scribal variation.
reflection_text.5:
The discussion remains polarised pronoun-first vs particle-first surface notation, with a stable majority and a persistent minority in round 4.

Working hypothesis retained: Host – Pron.P – V.encl – particle block – modal periphery, with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it, and бы the most peripheral member of the cluster. The core nucleus Host – мя – еси is again repeatedly affirmed by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 4 as invariant, e.g. *възлюби мя еси ли*.

Evidence reiterated in round 4:
* Functional tightness = left-to-right: enclitic personal/object pronoun most tightly bound, enclitic *běti* next, discourse particles next, conditional modal most peripheral.
* Pronoun–auxiliary nucleus мя > еси is stable.
* The two connective particles же and бо form a contiguous essentially interchangeable sub-block. Literary norm quoted as že > bo; manuscript/codicological norm bo > že. Both treated as scribal variants of same adjacency.
* бы is described as right-most element of the Wackernagel string. Two conventional renderings coexist:
  – textbook peripheral: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы / Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы
  – textbook post-auxiliary modal: Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, i.e. мя еси бы же бо, where бы is classed as immediate continuation of the auxiliary before the že/bo pair.

Public round 4 positions:
* Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 converge on the same canonical linearisation: W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with manuscript variant W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, and the closely related surface variant W – мя – еси – бы – же – бо. They explicitly state particle-first surface notations Host-že-bo-...-мя-...-еси-...-бы are a re-description of the same hierarchy with operators written next to the host and do not overturn linear мя > еси order on a single host.
* Colleague 10 persists with particle-first synthesis aligned to Laurentian/Hypatian strings, now refining to же бо еси бы мя / бо же еси бы мя, claiming operator-before-argument preference and that copula regularly intervenes between outer particle-modal block and accusative pronoun. Maintains majority strings мя еси же бо бы contradict particle-outermost examples, and argues particle > auxiliary/modal > pronoun sequence.
* Colleague 7 maintains particle-initial бо/же-first order, же бо бы еси мя / бо же бы мя еси, citing Laurentian/Hypatian particle immediacy. Now isolated.

Changes/notices round 4:
* No new manuscript citations beyond Laurentian/Hypatian/Lavra birch-bark; debate remains interpretive about classification of бы and linearisation of же/бо.
* Majority explicitly frames particle-first notation as descriptive reclassification, not a linear contradiction, reinforcing the pronoun > auxiliary > particle > бы layering.
* Colleague 10’s refinement keeps particles leftmost but now places еси before мя in the surface string, reducing but not eliminating conflict with pronoun-first nucleus.

Unresolved points still open:
* Же vs бо sub-order: canonical literary že > bo vs manuscript bo > že.
* Exact rank of бы relative to же/бо: most peripheral after particle pair vs immediately post-auxiliary before же/бо. Both мя еси же бо бы and мя еси бы же бо are presented as conventional variants of same pronoun > auxiliary > particle layering.
* Fundamental disagreement on whether the attested second-position order on one host is pronoun-initial or particle-initial; majority treats particle-first as notation, minority treats it as linear fact.

Current belief: canonical OCS/Old Russian second-position order for the set is pronoun first, auxiliary second, then the že/bo pair, then бы last: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with manuscript variant Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы, and closely related surface variant Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо. Essential layering pronoun > еси > particles > бы is retained, with že/bo interchange and бы periphery as remaining variable. Particle-first surface notation remains a minority view against the attested pronoun-auxiliary nucleus мя > еси.
reflection_text.3:
The second-position Wackernagel cluster for бы, же, еси, бо, мя is converging on a pronoun-first, auxiliary-second nucleus with a particle/modal block to the right. The majority core is now stable across rounds 1-4: Host – мя – еси – … with мя as leftmost enclitic and еси immediately following it, the pronoun-auxiliary nucleus мя > еси attested e.g. възлюби мя еси ли. Functional tightness hierarchy retained is Host > Pron.P > V.encl > particle block > modal periphery.

Inside the particle block the two discourse particles же and бо are contiguous and essentially interchangeable. Literary norm quoted as же > бо; бо > že is the regular older manuscript / codicological variant. Both sub-orders are accepted as local variation; essential layering is pronoun > auxiliary > že/бо.

бы remains the main source of variation but is described as rightmost / most peripheral. Majority surface citation is Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы, with same hierarchy rendered as Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы for the бо > že variant. The textbook variant Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо is treated as same pronoun-first, auxiliary-second, particle-final layering with бы classed as immediate continuation of the verbal enclitic before the že/бо pair, or as outermost modal of the block.

Round 4 public: Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 explicitly restate the tightness stack Host > enclitic argument > enclitic běti > discourse particle block > modal periphery, with Rank1 мя, Rank2 мя–еси nucleus, Rank3 же~бо interchangeable block, Rank4 бы rightmost. They explicitly identify particle-first surface notations Host-že-bo-…-мя-…-еси-…-бы as a re-description of the same hierarchy with operators written next to the host and not overturning the linear мя > еси order on a single host.

Minority positions persist:
* Colleague 10 maintains a particle-initial/operator-before-argument analysis, now refined to же бо еси бы мя / бо же еси бы мя, arguing Laurentian/Hypatian strings where discourse operators form immediate post-host unit and copula regularly intervenes between outer particle-modal block and accusative pronoun. He still denies a pronoun-first nucleus and keeps overall particle > auxiliary > modal > pronoun sequence, claiming majority strings contradict particle-outermost examples.
* Colleague 7 maintains же бо бы еси мя as best fit to Laurentian/Hypatian, operator unit же бо + scope-marking бы placed immediately after host before verbal/pronominal material, auxiliary and accusative pronoun forming tight inner pair once operator block fixed. He now notes compatibility with Colleague 10’s же бо еси бы мя surface adjustment and continues to exclude any pronoun-auxiliary nucleus.

No new manuscript evidence has overturned the pronoun-first nucleus. Colleague 10’s concession on еси-мя adjacency narrows his minority position but does not merge it with the majority.

Unresolved questions remaining:
* Canonical sub-order of же vs бо for the period, же > бо vs бо > že, and whether inversion is scribal variation.
* Canonical placement of бы: immediately post-auxiliary as modal continuation vs most peripheral member after the že/бо pair.
* Reconciling particle-first notations Host-že-bo-mja-esi-by with linear pronoun-first description; majority treats it as reclassification of same hierarchy, minority treats it as substantive.

Current working hypothesis: Host – мя – еси – же – бо – бы, with acknowledged variants Host – мя – еси – бо – же – бы and Host – мя – еси – бы – же – бо, all expressing pronoun > auxiliary > particle/modal layering with že/бо freely interchanged and бы rightmost, with particle-first proposals remaining an isolated minority.
reflection_text.4:
The Wackernagel second-position cluster remains the core problem. Functional classes are stable: мя = 1sg.acc. object pronoun enclitic, еси = 2sg. enclitic copula/auxiliary of *běti*, бы = conditional/modal particle, же = emphatic/connective particle, бо = causal/explanatory particle.

Round 4 consensus majority: 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 are now verbatim convergent on a tightness stack on one stressed host:
Host > enclitic argument > enclitic *běti* > discourse particle block > modal periphery.

Rank 1 most tightly bound: enclitic object pronoun
W – мя –

Rank 2: enclitic *běti*. The pronoun–auxiliary nucleus мя > еси is invariant core, e.g. възлюби мя еси ли.

Rank 3: discourse particle block to the right of the nucleus. же ‘also/and’ and бо ‘for’ are contiguous and essentially interchangeable. Literary norm quoted as же > бо with regular older codicological/scribal inversion бо > že.

Rank 4 most peripheral: conditional-modal бы closes the whole Wackernagel string to the right of the že/bo pair.

Canonical literary linearisation after ictus:
W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы
i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы  Host мя еси же бо бы.

Same layering cited with manuscript sub-order inversion
W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы  Host мя еси бо же бы
and with бы classed as immediate continuation of the verbal enclitic in textbook surface rendering
W – мя – еси – бы – же – бо  Host мя еси бы же бо.

The invariant OCS/Old Russian fact in this camp is pronoun-first, еси second, že ~ бо adjacent and interchangeable, бы rightmost. The particle-first surface notations Host-že-bo-...-мя-...-еси-...-бы are described as the same hierarchy re-described with operators written next to the host and do not overturn the linear мя > еси order on a single host.

Minority particle-first camp persists:
Colleague 10 maintains operator-before-argument preference, defends же бо еси бы мя / бо же еси бы мя as coherent with Laurentian/Hypatian strings, claims discourse operators form immediate post-host unit, copula intervenes between outer particle-modal block and accusative pronoun. Rejects unattested pronoun-auxiliary nucleus. Variability left on же ~ бо internal order and placement of бы immediately after auxiliary vs right edge of particle sub-block.
Colleague 7 maintains же бо бы еси мя as best fit for Laurentian/Hypatian, operator unit же бо plus scope-marking бы immediately after host before verbal/pronominal material, with auxiliary and accusative forming tight inner pair. Accepts minor surface adjustment же бо еси бы мя proposed by Colleague 10, preserving particle > auxiliary/modal > pronoun layering.

Unresolved questions persisting:
* Old Russian specifically vs Old Church Slavonic literary norm: is pronoun-first layering a general Slavonic norm or East Slavic textual reality?
* Classification of бы: modal particle peripheral to whole block vs modal tightly bound immediately after enclitic auxiliary еси.
* Stable же/бо sub-order: же > бо in most textbook citations, бо > že in many manuscript witnesses; both attested and treated as interchangeable locally.
* Relative order of auxiliary еси vs pronoun мя when particle-first description is adopted: Colleague 10 now keeps еси before мя, Colleague 7 keeps еси last.

No new manuscript evidence introduced in round 4; the round is reinforcement of pronoun-first majority with explicit equivalence claims and continuation of particle-first minority with slight softening to же бо еси бы мя.
reflection_text.6:
The deliberation remains centred on Wackernagel second-position internal tightness and the pronoun-first vs particle-first layering debate.

Stable majority core, reiterated by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 in round 4:
* Host > enclitic argument > enclitic *běti* > discourse particle block > modal periphery.
* Rank 1 most tightly bound is the 1 sg.acc. object enclitic pronoun мя, leftmost after the host: W – мя –
* Rank 2 is enclitic *běti* еси immediately after the pronoun. The pronoun-auxiliary nucleus мя > еси is treated as invariant, e.g. *възлюби мя еси ли*.
* Rank 3 is the discourse particle block to the right of the nucleus. же ‘also/and’ and бо ‘for’ are contiguous and essentially interchangeable in manuscripts; literary textbook norm quoted as же > бо with the regular older codicological/scribal variant бо > že.
* Rank 4 modal periphery: conditional-modal бы is the most peripheral member of the whole Wackernagel string, closing the cluster to the right of the же/бо pair.

Canonical linearisation given repeatedly:
W – мя – еси – же – бо – бы i.e. мя > еси > же > бо > бы
Host мя еси же бо бы.
Manuscript sub-order variant:
W – мя – еси – бо – же – бы i.e. мя еси бо же бы
Textbook modal-immediate variant:
W – мя – еси – бы – же – бо i.e. мя еси бы же бо
The invariant described as pronoun-first, еси-second, же/бо adjacent interchangeable, бы rightmost.

Particle-first minority persists:
* Colleague 7 holds же бо бы еси мя as best aligning with Laurentian/Hypatian strings where the discourse-operator unit же бо plus scope-marking бы is placed immediately after the host before verbal/pronominal material. Now notes compatibility with the minor surface adjustment же бо еси бы мя, arguing both preserve leftmost particle placement and exclude a pronoun-auxiliary nucleus.
* Colleague 10 maintains particle-first synthesis is most coherent with Laurentian/Hypatian/birch-bark evidence where discourse operators form an immediate post-host unit. Argues attested copula-pronoun adjacency once that unit is fixed favours же бо еси бы мя / бо же еси бы мя over же бо бы еси мя, because the copula regularly intervenes between the outer particle-modal block and the accusative pronoun. Rejects the pronoun-first nucleus мя > еси as opening the cluster and claims majority strings мя еси же бо бы contradict particle-outermost examples in earliest East Slavic material. Remaining variability is internal же ~ бо order and placement of бы immediately after auxiliary vs right edge of particle sub-block.

Unresolved tensions preserved:
* Exact relative order of же vs бо: attested both же > бо and бо > že; treated as scribal interchange.
* Classification/position of бы: majority keeps бы as rightmost peripheral element closing the cluster; sub-variant places бы immediately after еси before же/бо pair: мя еси бы же бо.
* Pronoun-first vs particle-first debate persists. Weight in rounds 1-4 is strongly pronoun-initial with мя leftmost and еси second, particles following, бы closing. Particle-first view is defended on manuscript surface strings with particles as leftmost Wackernagel material and operator-before-argument layering, with Colleague 10 partially converging toward hybrid же бо еси бы мя and Colleague 7 holding же бо бы еси мя.

Current belief keeps the dominant pronoun > auxiliary > particles > бы hierarchy with мя leftmost, еси immediately after it, же/бо adjacent interchangeable, бы rightmost, while retaining the minority particle-initial operator-before-argument claim and the noted manuscript variation for later evaluation.
